| Ruling | Storage rule |

| Q88a | Lane D evidence from Datomic dev storage is DIAGNOSTIC for every durable-readback, lost-ACK, P2 receipt and final acceptance obligation. Dev storage is H2 inside the transactor with H2's default 500 ms write delay, so an abrupt transactor stop can lose acknowledged transactions, which P2's 100% receipt bar does not allow. Acceptance runs on SQL storage on PostgreSQL (fsync on commit) with peers on a SELECT-only role (closes R28's R5, the peer writing storage). Dev storage stays allowed for development gates. This decides the storage half of Q78e without loosening any of Sam's bars; the other option R32 lists (accept a declared loss window) would loosen P2 and is Sam's alone. |

Gates: G1 88/88 with --previous; durability probes D1 (abrupt transactor stop) and D2 (abrupt Postgres stop) with zero lost ACKs, D0 the same on dev storage as the control; tenancy probe; erasure inventory smoke. |

## Contract 0.3.13: Datomic integration, content fingerprint admission and GS diagnostic policy

| Ruling | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Q91a | QLever-lane performance evidence (P1, P4, P5, GS) counts only from a server whose data sits mostly in a built base index with a delta bounded by a declared rebuild threshold. Every QLever receipt records base triple count, delta triple count and the delta in the blocks the measured scans touched. The lane's design (R2, R8, R13, R17) always assumed this; nothing built or measured it, and qlever-dev's base holds 1 triple. Earlier QLever latency numbers from delta-only servers are DIAGNOSTIC. |
| Q91b | qlever-dev is no longer reset with --fresh as a delta policy; delta growth on shared residents is handled by the rebuild loop of Q91c once it is qualified. |
| Q91c | EXP-QG1 (lab/experiments/EXP-QG1-qlever-generations/) builds the rebuild loop: phase 1 on an exclusive slot measures scan and join cost against delta size (monotonic and spread keys) on a 10M-triple base and picks the threshold; phase 2 rebuilds blue/green index generations from the broker log, with reader leases so one multi-request read stays on one generation, and checks Q89i byte identity across every swap. The feed stays the log. Bounding the delta per graph is rejected (all graphs share one server's blocks). |
| Q91d | The first rebuild-index runs on a copy of qlever-dev's data on an exclusive slot, not on the shared resident, because several reviews read qlever-dev live and upstream bug #3172 can make a rebuild fail. |
| Q93a | For seed reuse on every lane, the only evidence that grants admission is a content fingerprint (G0) read through the engine by the process that will measure, on the endpoint it measures, before its warm-up, compared with a digest pinned before the freeze began (and with O-DOMAIN where one exists). Every other observation (stop, settle, log tails, frontiers, inspect, stderr, timers, owner state, copy hashes, plan hashes, disk) is refusal-only or a diagnostic, and no decision reads a diagnostic. |

| Q94c | The GS background is the frozen TARGETS 2.1 trace through the W0 trace mapper (Q92k); the private writerTrace is retired; every measured window holds one burst and one maintenance event |
| Q94d | GS world admission follows Q93a: a G0 content fingerprint per run; a fresh scope or verified clone per run; store counts at start and end; on lane Q the Q91a counts |

Broker

| Ruling | Contract rule |
| --- | --- |
| Q72a | The flock helper runs detached in its own process group, ignores INT, TERM and HUP, and exits only on stdin EOF; when it exits for any reason the log fail-stops (every later append throws), and each append checks the helper is alive. A test kills the helper and Ctrl-Cs the holder's group and shows no second writer. |
| Q72b | Q67c applies to every broker read surface: a surface that answers in one request reads the marker in that request (a UNION with the marker triple, as pulls do); a surface that needs several requests (Datalog executor, dependencyState, native with awaitBasisMs) compares (incarnation, marker) before and after, and every fence and replay writes a new incarnation first. V-P2Q's live residual test (zero-downtime rewind between the probes) is a regression case. |
| Q72c | Rename reasons to the contract's strings now (`basis-not-reached`, `replica-unreachable`). Core tagged errors (Q67h) are required before the broker becomes a default, not for the default-off merge; until then no claim may close an obligation pinned to E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE or E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE. |
| Q72d | The A0 change with the option off is a correctness fix (main answers a basis above the published position) and stays. The frozen A0 control (Q46b) is re-frozen at the P2Q merge, and every matched comparison names the change. |
| Q72e | The synchronous whole-log replay per outage pull is a blocker for default, not for default-off; it is replaced by the Q58c store (recent_rows or a current index, on R25's design). Probes are coalesced into one in-flight probe per replica in this round. Tests import src through tsx, never dist. |
| Q72g | Every broker-mode wiring passes `awaitBasisMs: 2000` (the Q58a default) until the core native facade exists; receipts are measured at the claimed head. |
| Q84a | WAL, synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=ON on every non-readonly connection, checkpoint_fullfsync=ON, wal_autocheckpoint=0, journal_size_limit=16 MiB, locking NORMAL (not EXCLUSIVE); the single writer holds a SQLite exclusive lock on a separate broker.lock file for the life of the process (replaces the perl flock helper); assert SQLite >= 3.51.3 at open. |
| Q84b | One writer worker thread owns the read-write commit connection; one checkpointer thread runs wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) every 4 s on its own connection; four reader threads with readonly connections fed over MessagePort; the main thread never touches broker.db. Backstop: above 64 MiB of WAL the writer closes a gate, readers park between transactions, the writer runs RESTART. |
| Q84c | Every read transaction starts with `SELECT lsn, epoch, h FROM marker` and is served only when h <= B <= lsn, else routed to the source; one unit of work per transaction (one pull or one 64-subject page). Long work keeps its basis through a retention pin (pinBasis holds H <= B), never an open read transaction. |
| Q84d | H1's current rows live in broker.db as live_rows and retired_rows clustered by entity, written in the commit's own transaction, so W is always the snapshot's marker. |
| Q84e | Lock, open (recovery), PASSIVE (sync adopted frames), bump the epoch, run the marker and ACKED-sidecar cross-checks, then start readers; a mid-WAL corruption that SQLite recovers silently is caught by the ACKED sidecar. |

| Ruling | Contract rule |

| Q80a | O-OBS judges evidence only inside an evaluator-owned, contract-bound case and run context (obligation, case, witness kind, threshold ids, run id) and against collector objects the evaluator retained itself; evidence that only hashes itself is REFUSED. The collector and context format comes from R27. |
| Q80b | Each fault transition and each wait bound has a witness schema of source-bound events (start, end, readback) checked against retained objects; a label naming the transition or the duration is never evidence of it. |
| Q80c | Work ratios compare integer counters exactly against rational contract thresholds (cross-multiplication), never binary64. |
| Q82a | O-OBS enforces six kinds in trust order: EI engine-internal, TO transport-observed (a wire proxy in a separate process), HO host-observed (cgroup, /proc, sockets, file scans), DR durable read-back, HR harness-observed (caller-side fields only), CR reported by Triplex code (rejected; includes the Datomic gateway, the broker's own timestamps, and a counter inside the client process). `source.kind` is `<code>/<engine>/<sourceId>`. |
| Q82b | OBS-NO-MUTATION, OBS-PREABORT, OBS-CANCEL and OBS-ACK-ORDER pass only when two sources of different kinds agree. |
| Q82c | Evidence arrives as an obs-bundle/1 written by an observer sidecar per engine container that engine.mjs starts (never builder code): content-addressed raw chunks, a hash chain per stream, HMAC-SHA256 chunk headers under a per-run key the SUT never sees, a witness log of chain heads written only by orchestrator tooling, a clock bridge with stated uncertainty, and hash-pinned normalizer scripts that O-OBS reruns; records are recomputed from raw bytes, never accepted as given. Because every agent runs as one macOS user, acceptance additionally repeats the collection by the verifier (ACCEPTANCE 5.8); the bundle alone suffices only for screening. |
| Q82d | Every erasure-scan location first finds a canary written before the erasure with the same scanner, or the verdict is REFUSED (QLever's FSST-compressed vocabulary defeats plain grep). Observer outputs (QLever metrics log, XTDB DEBUG logs and spans, proxy captures, docker logs), old index generations and freed blocks join PROTECTED_COPY_INVENTORY. |
| Q82e | XTDB mutation evidence is the gauge node.tx.latestCompletedTxId, never source-log offsets (flushes and compaction append to the log); XTDB EXPLAIN ANALYZE attributes are JSON (scan_rows_read, scan_pages_used, scan_files_used), and the P4 harness's decoding (p4.mjs:29) is fixed to read them; QLever runs with --enable-metrics and its per-query metrics log on. Lane D CANCEL and PREABORT use host-observed per-thread /proc series of the gateway JVM plus the proxy (HO + TO). |

Continuation rules

| Ruling | Contract rule |
| --- | --- |
| Q70a | Every `cursorFrom` continuation is answered from the source read's start, scope and prefixes, whether or not the source had commits in flight; a continuation's own readStart is never consulted. |
| Q70b | A literal cursor token equal to a `nextCursor` that a read with commits in flight issued earlier in the same case continues that read per prefix; token bytes and the cursor vectors stay unchanged. Any other literal token keeps today's rule (the query's own read view). |
| Q70c | Q70b extends to every read: a literal cursor token equal to a `nextCursor` issued earlier in the same case by any read, in flight or not, continues that read (its start, scope and prefixes). Only a token no earlier read issued uses the query's own read view. This closes the F7 hole reached through a literal token. |
| Q70d | When several earlier reads issued the same token, the continuation follows the latest of them in case order. |
| Q70e | Prefixes whose pages did not issue the token are left out, the same as a prefix with no next cursor under `cursorFrom`. |
| Q70f | When the earlier reads that issued a literal token disagree in start, scope or per-prefix answers, the continuation fails closed with a typed X-NOT-MODELED "ambiguous literal token" (a fourth listed refusal site). Issuers with identical views continue as Q70d says. |
| Q70g | Q70c extends to the journal: a `transactions` call whose `after` equals a `next` that an earlier transactions page issued in the same case continues that read (its start and prefixes), one answer per prefix; an `after` no earlier page issued uses the call's own read view. |
| Q70h | Issuers are compared by view: start, scope, and the prefixes whose pages issued the token. Issuers with identical views and different page bodies (for example different limits reaching the same token) continue rather than refuse, because the continuation depends only on the view. |
| Q70i | Q70f's fail-closed rule applies to a journal `after` issued by disagreeing pages too ("ambiguous journal after"); Q70g matching requires the same journal scope. |
| Q70j | A `transactions` read decides which erasures are in flight from its own `scope` field, not from `cut.scope` or the default scope. |
| Q70k | Q70j applies to every read kind that takes a `scope` field (`transactions`, `transaction`, `transactionByCommand`, `transactionsForEntity`, `journalFacts`, `assertions`, `cutCatalog`, `history` with no cut): in-flight erasures come from the scope the read reads. Other kinds use their cut's scope. |
| Q70l | Every paged read kind continues by one rule. The oracle keeps a table of paged kinds and their continuation parameter and issued value (entityPage: `cursor`/`cursorFrom` and `nextCursor`; `transactions`: `after` and `next`; `transactionsForEntity`: `beforePosition` and `nextBeforePosition`, matched on the same entity, scope and `snapshotPosition`). A continuation value equal to one an earlier page of the same kind and key issued continues that read's view (Q70a-c, Q70g); disagreeing issuers refuse (Q70f, Q70i); identical views continue (Q70d, Q70h). A self-check fails if any query kind whose output carries a `next*` field is missing from the table, so a new paged kind cannot be left on the old rule. |
| Q70m | `after`, `beforePosition` and any other integer continuation parameter must be a JSON integer; a string, a float or a negative value makes the case malformed (exit 2), never a crash or a FAIL exit. Matching uses the parsed integer. |
| Q70n | The Q70l completeness check runs every query kind registered in `run.QUERIES` on generated cases and inspects the actual output (top level, pages and nested objects) for any `next*` key; a kind whose output carries one and is not in `CONTINUATIONS` fails, and a kind that cannot be exercised fails conservatively. Static source matching may stay as an extra check, never as the only one. Negative controls: a computed key, a helper in another module, a nested dictionary. |
| Q70o | `cursorFrom.page` is an integer continuation parameter under Q70m: a JSON integer from 0 to the last page index, otherwise the case is malformed (exit 2); invalid reference shapes raise the oracle's input error, never an uncaught exception. |

Evaluator integrity

| Ruling | Contract rule |
| --- | --- |
| Q75a | At the start of every run, every evaluator-side file the run executes (claim.mjs, lib.mjs, gate.mjs, the reference and oracle runner files) is compared with its git blob at the evaluator's commit, read with `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`; a mismatch refuses the run and marks the checkout poisoned (EVALUATOR-TAMPERED) until restored from git. An edit made and restored inside one run stays on the named unprotected list until EXP-G03 isolates builds. |
| Q75b | Every oracle copy and every other trusted byte is read, hashed and copied before the first candidate process runs; the evaluator's git runs with `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` and checks each blob against its tree entry's object id. |
| Q75c | An oracle is pinned only when the contract lists sha256 for every runner file; COMPILED oracles (O-CONTRACT) are pinned that way through the contract's own outputs. A claim that depends on any oracle without such a list is DIAGNOSTIC (Q59e literally). build_contract.py's contractBlockers and claim.mjs's follow the same rule in contract 0.3.11. |
| Q75d | The identity records each resolved binary children run (node, pnpm, python3): path, sha256 and version; children run with PATH pinned to the recorded toolchain directory. |
| Q75e | The identity walk uses lstat, refuses any symlink that resolves outside the checkout, and hashes file modes; configuration the evaluator does not apply is recorded as unbound, not hashed as if applied. |
| Q75f | Every child process gets a fresh HOME and TMPDIR. |
| Q75g | A row comparator applies to each `queries[i]` entry's `result` (or its `inFlight.acceptable[j].result`) inside an O-REPLAY answer; `commandOutcomes` and `state` compare exactly. Contract 0.3.11 states this; until then those cases stay UNCOMPARABLE (fail closed). |
| Q75h | Following compiled Q67h, `cause` is optional; when present it must be a structured object with `_tag` or `message`. |
| Q75i | The run keeps the set of evidence hashes it wrote and requires every one at the end (deletion detected); every return path carries GATE-NOT-RUN from the run's start; end checks run inside the try. admitCore returns DIAGNOSTIC for `kind: "promotion"`, and admit_claim in the reference does the same in 0.3.11. |
| Q75j | The unprotected list names F1's in-run restore, setsid, TOCTOU, no filesystem or network isolation; "double fork escapes" is corrected (it is killed). Q67i's "CMP-EXACT" reads as CMP-EXACT-VALUE; no comparator is plain byte equality, and hash equality applies only to case-result/1 documents. |
| Q81a | At the end of a run the evaluator re-checks every case input it handed out (present, same bytes) along with the evidence set; a deleted or rewritten input after its last use refuses the run (INPUT-TAMPERED). The guarantee is kept, not narrowed. |

| Q76d | The C8 follow-up wires `countSimplePaths` into WL20 supports on both lanes, so supports are general rather than path lengths 1-3. |
| Q76e | Maintained queries publish only from the change feed consumer (P3), never from a read; until that consumer exists, `query()` answers directly. |
| Q76f | XTDB G1/G2 receipts for C8 are rerun on an exclusive slot after V-X02's; the overloaded-dev receipts stay as diagnostic. |
| Q77a | Every accepted recursion budget is enforced with a typed refusal and never a partial or over-budget success: a confirmation read may not extend the answer past maxRounds; ruleClosure enforces maxRounds and maxVisited (or rejects budget fields it does not support). maxDepth keeps its Datalog meaning. |
| Q77b | Path counting uses iterative DP over DAGs and an explicit stack for bounded cyclic enumeration; pathSteps refusal stays typed. |
| Q77c | The write counter positively classifies every operation it forwards; any multipart, prepared, portal or other operation it cannot classify counts as a write (or is refused). Classifications of prepared statements and portals survive tally resets, and Execute operations are what is counted. |

Lane D

| Ruling | Contract rule |
| --- | --- |
| Q78a | Datomic Pro 1.0.7745 (Apache 2.0 binaries, Java 17+), dev storage inside the transactor for DA00-DA02; SQL storage is a later arm only if io-stats show peer cache misses loading the transactor. The zip's sha256 is pinned by the lab, the bundled peer jar is cross-checked against Maven Central's sha1 and PGP signature. No Datomic source exists, so lane D has no engine-repair track; gaps get workarounds. |
| Q78b | `tx2-datomic-dev` (2.75 GiB: transactor heap 640m, gateway heap 1g) is a parkable resident: only the orchestrator parks it (`engine.mjs down`, volume kept). Lane D slot runs and lane X/Q exclusive-slot runs do not overlap with it running. |
| Q78c | A thin Clojure gateway on the official Peer API speaking HTTP/1.1 + JSON with every value tagged (longs and entity ids as decimal strings); the gateway rejects query functions outside an allowlist (C8 floor). Rejected: peer-server with the undocumented Client wire protocol; the legacy REST server. |
| Q78d | One Datomic database per Triplex scope; each assertion is a fact entity (`:f/id`, `:f/subject`, `:f/live`, `:f/attr`, one typed value attribute, valid-time bounds); commit metadata on the transaction entity; retraction retracts `:f/live`; a latest-basis read uses the current db, a past basis `as-of`, reads in a transaction `d/with`. One `:db/cas` per entity per transaction (Jepsen: operations inside one transaction apply as if concurrent). |
| Q85a | Database creation for a scope is idempotent and never resets or lowers an existing scope position; concurrent creates converge on one database with its position intact. |
| Q85b | The gateway accepts every scope name the public Triplex constructor can produce (mapped to a Datomic database name by a documented, reversible encoding) and nothing else. |
| Q85c | Every image build starts from a fresh context that contains only verified inputs listed in the input hash; a reused or dirty context refuses the build. |
| Q85d | The TypeScript and JVM codecs share one specification of each value kind's range and representation, with a shared test vector set; a value either codec cannot represent is refused by both. |
| Q88a | Lane D evidence from Datomic dev storage is DIAGNOSTIC for every durable-readback, lost-ACK, P2 receipt and final acceptance obligation. Dev storage is H2 inside the transactor with H2's default 500 ms write delay, so an abrupt transactor stop can lose acknowledged transactions, which P2's 100% receipt bar does not allow. Acceptance runs on SQL storage on PostgreSQL (fsync on commit) with peers on a SELECT-only role (closes R28's R5, the peer writing storage). Dev storage stays allowed for development gates. This decides the storage half of Q78e without loosening any of Sam's bars; the other option R32 lists (accept a declared loss window) would loosen P2 and is Sam's alone. |
| Q88b | Lane D moves to SQL storage in EXP-DA04 (brief lab/experiments/EXP-DA04-sql-storage/BRIEF.md) before the DA03 NS smoke: resident pair Postgres 0.5 GiB plus Datomic 2.25 GiB in the existing 2.75 GiB budget (fallback 3.0 GiB if G1 runs short), exclusive lane D slot 4.0 GiB with the resident pair parked. Gates: G1 88/88 with --previous; durability probes D1 (abrupt transactor stop) and D2 (abrupt Postgres stop) with zero lost ACKs, D0 the same on dev storage as the control; tenancy probe; erasure inventory smoke. |
| Q88c | Crypto-shredding is the primary PII erasure on every lane D storage; Datomic excision in batches of about 2,000 to 3,000 datoms is the second layer; keys live in their own Postgres schema so key deletion can be shown by scanning table files and WAL. |

Exact queries

| Ruling | Contract rule |
| --- | --- |
| Q79a | Every SQL hazard guard runs on the same comment-aware token stream as the envelope, recognises quantified comparisons including the bare-expression operand, and keeps `UNION ALL` / `SELECT ALL` and supported subqueries; public-provider regression cases for the comment and bare forms. |
| Q79b | Checked int64 arithmetic yields a typed failure in the Effect error channel, never a defect; tests assert Fail (not Die) and recovery with catchTag in both languages. |
| Q79c | Exact Datalog arithmetic (the five exact compute operators and anything downstream) never lowers through DECIMAL to BIGINT; it keeps the exact result as text through range checks and decoding, or refuses with a typed error until exact lowering exists. This is Sam's "no silent precision loss" rule and applies to core's compiler for every lane that uses it. |
| Q79d | With the language switch unset, behaviour is main's; changing the default needs its own qualification and a ruling. |
| Q79e | The quantified-comparison guard classifies the operand by a small grammar, not by listed shapes: any parenthesized query expression (SELECT, VALUES, and set operations UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT with or without ALL, at any nesting of parentheses, with comments anywhere) is a subquery and is admitted if it contains no nested unsafe comparison; anything else is refused. Tests are generated from the grammar's combinations (each form at depths 1-3, with and without comments) and each generated query is checked against XTDB's own answer, next to the round-2 rejections. |
| Q79f | The X02 guard treats comments exactly as the pinned XTDB lexer does (SqlLexer.g4:12 defines BLOCK_COMMENT recursively): balanced nested block comments are consumed at any depth, an unterminated comment is an error, and the guard's tokenizer must agree with the lexer on every identifier boundary, including dollar-bearing, quoted and Unicode identifiers. Where the guard and the lexer disagree, the query is refused, never passed. |

### 0.1.0-draft

First draft (88 obligations). Superseded.

## 1. How to read this contract

- **One obligation is one binary fact.** It has an id, a statement, lanes, case selections, oracles, entrypoints, profiles, a closure (rules, modes, thresholds), mutation controls, the PLAN contracts it traces, sources, a grounding label and a verifier mode.
- **Every status is OPEN.** No acceptance receipt exists for any obligation.
- **Authority for goals and targets.** `lab/SCOPE.md`, `lab/NORTH-STAR.md`, `lab/TARGETS.md` and `lab/research/SAM-pasted-numbers-2026-11-07.md` (Sam, 2026-11-07), compiled with `RULINGS.md` into `obligations.json`. Correctness is the floor on every priority: a fast wrong answer scores zero.
- **Values this contract chose.** Thresholds whose source says `derived`, the reader read mix and window lengths in `load-contract.json`, and the A0 allowances in `budgets.json` are values no source states; they are fixed so evaluation is mechanical, and changing one is a contract version.
- **Artifacts.** `obligations.json` (authority), `load-contract.json`, `budgets.json`, `capability-matrix.md`, this file. All generated.

## 2. Done predicate (PLAN v1.1 section 1)

```
done(T) = for one identified integrated profile T per surface
          AND over lanes { xtdb-xtql, xtdb-sql, qlever-sparql, datomic-datalog }
          AND over sections { G1..G10, R, S, L }
            closed(section, lane, T)
          with every receipt FRESH on T (no carry-forward into final acceptance)

 retained evidence --> VC / VA / VM / VV validity --> closure rules recompute verdicts --> obligation
   (runs/objects)       (acyclic: VC <- VA <- VM, VV)    from retained bytes             --> section --> lane --> done
```


Status algorithm:

```
for each lane L and integrated profile T:
  for each obligation O with L in O.lanes:
    key = L if O.receiptScope == 'lane' else (O.layer, T.composition[O.layer].engine, imageDigest, configSha256, slot)  # RULINGS Q28
    if O.closure.params.keyByNativeLanguage: key = (key, receipt.nativeLanguage) and only receipts whose nativeLanguage is L's language count for L  # RULINGS Q39b
    A = acceptance receipts for (O.id, key) on T that pass VA (using VC records they cite)
    closed(O, L, T) = O.grounding != 'policy-pending' and every case set of O is pinned
                      and A non-empty and every rule in O.closure.rules holds by its recompute
                      and VV-valid verifier coverage exists per VERIFIER_MODES[verifierMode(O)]
                      and every gate in O.closure.params.gates holds (GATES; an unknown or null input fails closed)
  closed(section, L, T) = all closed(O, L, T) for O with section in O.goals
done(T) = closed for every section and lane, with every receipt fresh on T (APPLICABILITY.finalAcceptance)
```

**Lane accounting.** Every read substep records exactly one language: xtql (native.select), sql (selectSql), sparql (QLever native), datomic-datalog (Datomic query and pull). A lane receipt counts a task only when every relational substep is in the lane's language. A task with a relational substep in another language, or with a host step not listed below, counts for neither XTDB language.

| Permitted host step | Source | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HS-NORMALIZE | RULINGS Q3 | A declared normalization step that reads no data: arithmetic or classification over values already returned by native substeps of the same task (for example BigInt subtraction of two returned sums). It is declared in the frozen task recipe, recorded in the trace, and its time is counted inside the task's measured call. |
| HS-FRONTIER | PLAN C8 | C8 frontier control for recursive reads, limited to the operations in FRONTIER_RULES. All relational evaluation stays native at one fixed cut. |

**C8 frontier control (HS-FRONTIER).**

- Permitted host operations: deduplicate returned frontier ids; subtract the visited set from the new frontier; test termination (empty frontier, maxRounds reached, maxRecursiveRows reached); bind the next frontier as query parameters, chunked so each native query stays within its declared parameter bound; count rows and rounds against the bounds.
- Forbidden host operations: filtering on values, types, entity types or time; joins between returned relations; visibility, cut or valid-time evaluation; negation, aggregation, ordering or pagination of answers; any read that does not go through the lane's native language.
- fixedCut: Every round runs at the same captured basis (scope, P, optional R, V); each round's trace records that basis and the evaluator checks they are identical.
- bounds: maxRounds and maxRecursiveRows are declared per task. Reaching a bound fails with the typed recursion-limit error (ERROR_TABLE E-RECURSION-LIMIT) and returns no partial answer.
- cost: Host frontier time and peak host memory are counted inside the task's measured cost and reported per round.
- noMutation: No round writes engine state (engine-side mutation count unchanged across the read).
- accounting: A task whose host steps are only HS-FRONTIER (and HS-NORMALIZE) operations counts as pure in the lane's language.

### 3.2 Legacy signed-64 golden vectors (RULINGS Q31j)

Follow-up EXP-G02 (RULINGS Q32b): QLever in-range companion vectors by an independent golden author. For every golden vector (or vector case) that commits an integer outside QLever's accepted range, the evaluator applies the compiled lane outcome in LEGACY_LANE_OUTCOMES instead of the vector's single expected answer: XTDB commits and keeps the original answer; QLever's qualified write routes reject the command with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE before any mutation (RULINGS Q23, Q31j). ## 4. Frozen semantic tables (expected-answer authority)

A later change in production behavior never changes an expected answer automatically; it needs a contract version.

### 4.0 Value kinds and the numeric rule (NUMERIC)

| Kind | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| string | exact codepoint sequence; ill-formed UTF-16 rejected with E-INVALID-VALUE |
| integer | exact; every lane accepts at least [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1]; each lane declares its accepted range (LANE_INTEGER_RANGE); a value outside the lane's range fails the write with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE and leaves no residue; never wrapped, widened or rounded |
| number | binary64 for approximate, deterministic values only (for example a risk score), never business values; stored and read bit-exact; NaN and infinities rejected |
| decimal | value kind for money and business decimals (RULINGS Q18 as amended by Q35b, DECIMAL_RULES): the attribute declares precision and scale; one stored representation on both lanes, the TDK1 key (value-determined, order-preserving, channel decimal_order_v1) plus derived canonical text; exact storage and round trip; more fractional digits than the scale fail with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION, a value beyond the precision with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW, never rounded; its own family; arithmetic in the TypeScript kernel with exact decimal arithmetic |
| boolean | exact |
| datetime | exact epoch-millisecond instant including fractional milliseconds; values needing nanoseconds use ISO strings (NUMERIC table) |
| ref | exact target id |
| json | exact text with key order kept; canonical form for identity |
| blob | exact descriptor (mimeType, size, filename) |

| Engine | Declared integer range | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| xtdb | [-2^63, 2^63-1] (BIGINT) | values inside are stored exactly; the lane may accept the whole core integer range |
| datomic | [-2^63, 2^63-1] (long; unqualified until DA00) | exact tagged decimal strings through the gateway; hard error outside the range |
| qlever | [-2^59, 2^59-1] (60-bit native integers; lexical channel exact) | values outside are rejected at write with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE before any engine mutation (TARGETS section 3) |

Every lane accepts at least [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1]. Every attribute used in a range rule (for example 'pay rate at or above 16.50', 'hours over 40') has an order-preserving comparison on every surface that serves the rule: native exact types inside their exact range, or a documented order-preserving channel.

**Decimal (RULINGS Q18).** declaration: every decimal attribute declares precision p (total significant digits) and scale s (fractional digits), 0 <= s <= p. storage: every declared precision and scale (both lanes) -> the TDK1 key in channel decimal_order_v1 (authoritative, decodes exactly) plus derived canonical text at the declared scale; QLever also keeps its lexical channel for parity with other kinds (RULINGS Q35b, amending Q18). oneRepresentation: the decimal kind has exactly one stored representation; Q18's scaled-integer path no longer applies; money modeled as integer cents uses the integer kind (RULINGS Q35b). reject: a value with more than s fractional digits (counted on the value, so 16.500 fits scale 2, R-DEC-3) fails with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION; a value beyond the declared precision or 38 digits fails with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW; -0.00 in any spelling is refused with E-INVALID-VALUE (R-DEC-2); a decimal on an attribute not declared decimal is E-INVALID-VALUE (R-DEC-0); every rejection leaves no residue; never rounded or truncated (RULINGS Q33b, Q35e). wireShape: {"type": "decimal", "value": "16.50"} (R-DEC-1); a value with extra trailing zeros is returned at the declared scale (16.500 at scale 2 reads back as 16.50) while the original input text is still captured (Q22, R-DEC-3). toDecimal: toDecimal(number, p, s, rounding) starts from the number's exact binary expansion, then applies the caller's scale and rounding (R-DEC-6). avg: AVG over decimal is preflight E-DECIMAL-AVG unless written as divide(SUM, COUNT, scale, rounding) (R-DEC-7); decimal divide is modeled by the oracle (follow-up EXP-O03, R-DEC-5). family: decimal is its own family, ordered between number and datetime (CARD_MANY_ORDER); 1.50 and 1.5 are one value. comparison: CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS: comparison with integer or number is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless the query converts explicitly. arithmetic: TypeScript kernel, exact decimal arithmetic; engine-side decimal arithmetic only where a projection needs it (RULINGS Q19). inputCapture: the writer captures the caller's original typed input before any normalization; tests assert nothing was rounded before capture (DEC-INPUT-CAPTURE, M-DECIMAL-PRECAPTURE-ROUND). kernelMaxDigits: 38.

**Decimal operations (RULINGS Q22).**

| Id | Operation | Result scale | Result precision | Error | Case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DO-ADD | a + b, a - b (decimal(p1, s1), decimal(p2, s2)) | max(s1, s2) | max(p1 - s1, p2 - s2) + max(s1, s2) + 1 | E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW when the result exceeds the target's declared precision or 38 digits | DEC-OP-ADD |
| DO-MUL | a * b | s1 + s2 | p1 + p2 | E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW when the result exceeds the target's declared precision or 38 digits | DEC-OP-MUL |
| DO-DIV | divide(a, b, scale, rounding) with rounding one of half-even, half-up, down | the named scale | the target's declared precision | E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO for b = 0; E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW beyond the precision; the one place rounding happens, and only when the caller names it | DEC-OP-DIVIDE |
| DO-BARE-DIV | a / b on decimals | - | - | preflight E-DECIMAL-BARE-DIVIDE | DEC-OP-BARE-DIVIDE |
| DO-ROUND | round(x, s, rounding) | s | p - (s_x - s) when s < s_x; p + (s - s_x), capped at 38, when s > s_x (exact: appends zeros, never refused); p when s = s_x | E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW only when a carry exceeds the precision or the 38-digit cap | DEC-OP-ROUND |
| DO-CMP | = != < <= > >= between decimals | - | - | none; compares exact numeric value (1.50 = 1.5) | DEC-OP-COMPARE |
| DO-SUM | SUM over decimals (kernel; engine side only where a projection needs it) | max scale of the inputs | 38 | E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW when the exact total exceeds 38 digits | DEC-OP-SUM |

**Decimal conversions and scale evolution (RULINGS Q22).**

| Id | Rule | Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DC-I2D | integer to decimal(p, s): exact when the integer fits p - s digits, else E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW | DEC-CV-INT-TO-DEC |
| DC-D2I | decimal to integer (toInteger): only when the fraction is zero, else E-DECIMAL-FRACTION unless the caller writes round(x, 0, rounding) first; a whole decimal outside the integer range is E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW (RULINGS Q43g) | DEC-CV-DEC-TO-INT |
| DC-D2N | decimal to number: only through toNumber(x) (named, lossy, one correctly rounded binary64) | DEC-CV-DEC-TO-NUM |
| DC-N2D | number to decimal: only through toDecimal(x, p, s, rounding); NaN and infinities never occur (rejected at write) | DEC-CV-NUM-TO-DEC |
| DC-T2D | text to decimal at the write boundary: the canonical decimal grammar only; more fractional digits than s (counted on the value) is E-DECIMAL-FRACTION and more than p - s integer digits is E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW, never rounded | DEC-CV-TEXT-TO-DEC |
| DC-IMPLICIT | no implicit conversion between decimal and integer or number in any expression; mixing them is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY (CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS) | DEC-CROSS-FAMILY-PREFLIGHT |
| DS-WIDEN | a declaration change that admits every existing value is metadata-only: TDK1 keys depend on the value alone, so Q31g's key-compatibility condition always holds and no key is rewritten; stored values read back with the new declared scale (RULINGS Q35b, superseding Q31g's migration path) | DEC-SCALE-WIDEN |
| DS-WIDEN-MIGRATE | a change under which some existing value no longer fits (for example integer digits p - s shrink) validates every live and historical value first and fails atomically with E-DECIMAL-NARROWING before any mutation; no key rewrite is ever needed | DEC-SCALE-WIDEN-MIGRATE |
| DS-NARROW | narrowing precision or scale is a migration that fails atomically with E-DECIMAL-NARROWING, before any mutation, if any live or historical value would lose digits | DEC-SCALE-NARROW |

**Decimal test classes (RULINGS Q22).** DEC-ADJACENT-LARGE: adjacent 38-digit decimals (differing in the last digit) stay distinct and ordered on every surface; DEC-NEGATIVE: negative values, including order across zero; DEC-ZERO: 0, 0.00 and -0.00 are one value; DEC-SCALE-BOUNDARY: values with exactly s fractional digits and exactly p - s integer digits accepted; one more rejected; DEC-INTERMEDIATE: arithmetic intermediates are exact (no rounding before the final result); DEC-EVERY-PATH: every query and serialization path (Triples, repository, native, raw hatch, feed, journal, backup and restore) round-trips exactly; DEC-ORDER-KEY-INDEPENDENT: an independent checker compares the order-key byte order with exact numeric order over the whole CS-DECIMAL corpus; DEC-INPUT-CAPTURE: the writer's captured input equals the caller's original typed input before normalization.

**Wire exactness (RULINGS Q30).**

| Id | Rule | Source | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WR-JSON | a user-supplied JSON value containing -0, a non-finite number, or a number that does not read back as written (its shortest round-trip binary64 rendering differs from the given text in canonical form, RULINGS Q33a: 0.1 accepted, 9007199254740993 rejected) is rejected at every qualified write route with E-INEXACT-JSON-NUMBER (InvalidTripleError / invalid-value, detail inexact-json-number), never normalized; the guard runs before CanonicalJson, whose canonical identity is unchanged; approximateNumbers: reject applies recursively inside List and Struct; the guard applies to user JSON only: JSON that Triplex generates (journal changes, metadata) never passes through it, and the journal encodes typed values losslessly, so a number -0 assertion commits, journals, replays and reads back bit-exact (RULINGS Q34c, AMB-04) | RULINGS Q30a, Q33a, Q34c | WIRE-JSON-NEGZERO, WIRE-JSON-NONFINITE, WIRE-JSON-INEXACT, WIRE-JSON-NESTED-LIST, WIRE-JSON-NESTED-STRUCT, WIRE-JSON-BEFORE-CANONICAL, Q33-JSON-READBACK, WIRE-JOURNAL-NUMBER-NEGZERO-ROUNDTRIP |
| WR-INSTANT | an instant given as -0 is rejected with E-NEGATIVE-ZERO-INSTANT (NoNegativeZero), never turned into 0 | RULINGS Q30b | WIRE-INSTANT-NEGZERO |
| WR-X-ENCODINGS | ProjectionSpec pins the XTDB encodings F02 proved exact: card-many DOUBLE and integer lists are written as ARRAY[CAST(? **Decimal order key TDK1 (RULINGS Q35).** channel: decimal_order_v1. source: lab/research/R20-order-preserving-decimal-encodings.md section 6; RULINGS Q35a. summary: value-determined, order-preserving (TDK1): zero o; positive p LL I F (LL two-digit integer-digit count, I without leading zeros, F without trailing zeros); negative n (99-L) comp(I) comp(F) z with comp(d) = 9 - d. alphabet: 0123456789nopz. inputGrammar: -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?; refused: +1, 01, 1., .5, 1e3, whitespace, non-ASCII digits, negative zero in any spelling. decode: parse strictly, then render the sign, I or 0, and when s > 0 a '.' followed by F right-padded with zeros to s digits. order: codepoint order of keys equals numeric order; the alphabet [0-9nopz] makes ICU order equal codepoint order on QLever and byte order on XTDB (no collation on 2.2.0). useConstraints: keys are never concatenated into a composite string and never used for prefix queries (p0212 is a prefix of p02125); only whole-key equality and ordered comparison, as a separate sort column (RULINGS Q35d). versioning: a future encoding gets a new channel name and a migration (RULINGS Q35c). limits: maximum precision 38 (TDK1 has headroom to 99 integer digits); no native XTDB DECIMAL lane: one verification path (RULINGS Q35e). kernelNote: if the kernel uses decimal.js or big.js, rounding tests cover their signed zero (RULINGS Q35e).

**Outbox publication (RULINGS Q38f).** sweepFrames: provisional: a sweep page may publish up to 64 results in one frame: one atomic outbox commit per frame, each result its own work item with its own delivery identity (RULINGS Q68c, Q38f). sweepFrameMaxResults: 64. deliveryKey: (id, publication sequence). sequence: durable per work-item id; increments when the payload to publish differs from the latest published payload for that id, so R1 to R2 to R1 publishes three deliveries (1650, 1700, 1650) and the receiver never suppresses the return. contentVersion: hashes (release, inputs, payload); recorded, never the delivery identity. atomicity: publication state (sequence and latest published payload) is persisted atomically with its outbox record. recovery: unacknowledged deliveries survive crashes and replay with their original identity. publishRule: per id the sequence starts at 1; publish (id, seq + 1) when the id was never published, when the payload's canonical bytes differ from the latest published payload, or when the id reappears after a recorded retirement (even with an unchanged payload); version is content identity only (RULINGS Q40c, Q40h). basisOrder: per subject the outbox applies an evaluation only if its basis is newer than the last applied one: greater basis.tx, or equal tx with a valid time not earlier; an older-basis evaluation publishes nothing (RULINGS Q40d). retirement: when a work item id disappears from a subject's outputs, the outbox records its retirement; a later reappearance publishes a new sequence even if the payload equals the last published one (RULINGS Q40h). liveOnly: a delivery's subject comes from the evaluation record; only live reconciles at the current basis are passed to publish; previews (GS.11) and past-valid-time audit evaluations never are (RULINGS Q44c). atomicUnit: per subject, the basis guard, retirement state, publication sequence, latest published payload and the outbox records are persisted in one atomic write under the subject's compare-and-set; the guard advances on empty and unchanged evaluations too (RULINGS Q42c). receivers: receivers apply deliveries per id by publication sequence: a state projection records the highest sequence applied and ignores any lower one (never regresses); an effect that needs every transition processes sequences in order and recovers gaps from the outbox before applying a later one; receiver deduplication is persisted atomically with the receiver's state or effect, or the recipient is idempotent by (id, seq); receivers exist from the first publication or are seeded with a state snapshot (RULINGS Q42b, Q44d). operations: W0 defines publish(state, evaluations) -> {deliveries, state} and receive(state, deliveries) -> state as pure operations so O-DOMAIN gives the expected outbox and receiver state (RULINGS Q40c, Q42b).

| Case | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| OB-CORRECTION-REVERT | a correction that reverts a payload to its previous value publishes a new sequence (RULINGS Q40c) |
| OB-OLDER-BASIS-NO-DELIVERY | a newer-basis R2 evaluation followed by an older-basis R1 evaluation yields no delivery (RULINGS Q40d) |
| OB-RETIREMENT-REAPPEAR | a work item that disappears and later reappears with the same payload publishes a new sequence (a second FNC notice is delivered, RULINGS Q40h) |
| OB-PREVIEW-NOT-PUBLISHED | preview (GS.11) and past-valid-time audit evaluations are never passed to publish (RULINGS Q44c) |
| OB-RELEASE-ROLLBACK | activate R1, R2, R1 over unchanged business facts: three deliveries with sequences 1, 2, 3 and payloads 1650, 1700, 1650 |
| OB-CRASH-BEFORE-DELIVERY | crash after the outbox record and publication state commit but before delivery: replay delivers the same (id, publication sequence) exactly once |
| OB-UNCHANGED-ACTIVATION-RECOVERY | an activation that leaves the payload unchanged while an earlier delivery is still unacknowledged after a crash: nothing new is published and the pending delivery replays with its original identity |
| OB-ATOMIC-STATE | a crash between the outbox record and its publication state is impossible: both or neither are visible |

| CV-F2I | toInteger(number): only explicit; the value must be integral and inside integer, else E-INVALID-CONVERSION; -0.0 converts to 0 | toInteger(3.0) = 3; toInteger(3.5) = E-INVALID-CONVERSION; toInteger(9223372036854775808.0) = E-INVALID-CONVERSION |
| CV-T2I | CAST text to integer: canonical decimal only (optional leading '-', no '+', no leading zeros except '0', no '-0'), inside integer, else E-INVALID-CONVERSION or E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW | '9223372036854775808' = E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW; '-9223372036854775808' = -9223372036854775808; '01' = E-INVALID-CONVERSION; '+1' = E-INVALID-CONVERSION |
| CV-NONE | no implicit conversion between families anywhere (filters, joins, group keys, aggregates) |  |

### 4.3 Comparisons and group identity

| Id | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CMP-SAME | same family: exact comparison (integer as integers, binary64 by IEEE value, text by Unicode codepoint sequence, datetime by instant, boolean false < true, ref by id codepoints) | exact typing |
| CMP-NUMERIC-CONST | an untyped numeric constant compares by numeric value with number and datetime values (number 7 and datetime 7 both equal 7); text '7' is not equal | testkit 'datalog equality predicates compare numeric values as numbers' (packages/testkit/src/index.ts:721) |
| CMP-INT-FLOAT | integer versus number: equality is false and they never share a group; an ordered comparison across them is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless converted explicitly | RULINGS Q8d (core silent for stored integer versus number) |
| CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS | every comparison between decimal and integer or number, equality included, and any grouping or set operation mixing them, is a preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless the query converts explicitly (DECIMAL_CONVERSIONS); there is no false or null result | RULINGS Q18, Q22 |
| CMP-CROSS-FAMILY-ORDERED | every ordered comparison across type families is a preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY, never false; equality across families is false except where a ruling makes it an error (decimal, CMP-DECIMAL-CROSS) | RULINGS Q33d (R-CMP-3); Q14d |
| CMP-IDENTITY | entity ids and ref identities compare only with text or ref constants; a numeric or boolean constant is never equal and != is true | testkit 'datalog equality keeps identity bindings string-typed' |
| CMP-UNTYPED-STRING | an untyped string constant matches string and ref values; a typed ref constant matches only ref values | testkit 'datalog untyped strings match string and ref values while typed refs stay exact' |
| CMP-BOOL-INT | boolean true and integer 1 are distinct values and distinct groups | packet oracle identity() (event_oracles.py: bool true vs i64 one) |
| CMP-NEGZERO | -0.0 and +0.0 are one value for identity, grouping and set membership; when supports differ only in representation, the returned representation is the one from the support with the lowest (recordedPosition, operation index) (amended by RULINGS Q21 AMB-08; assertion ids are generated per lane and are never used); a single-assertion read returns the stored representation | RULINGS Q14b; packages/core/src/content/CanonicalJson.ts:77 |

### 4.4 Aggregates

| Id | Rule | Examples | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AG-SUM-I | SUM over integers, where a surface or projection offers it: exact total over the solution rows (bag of distinct bindings); E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW only when the final total is outside the integer range; partial sums never wrap. Engine-side sums are required only for projections that declare them (G5.agg.projection-sums); per-subject sums run in the kernel | [2^62, 2^62] = E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW; [2^62, 2^62, -2^62] = 4611686018427387904; [2^58, 2^58, 2^58] = 864691128455135232 | RULINGS Q8a, NUMERIC; compiler.ts SUM over DECIMAL(32,0) |
| AG-SUM-F | SUM over number, where offered: the correctly rounded value of the exact sum (one rounding), independent of evaluation order | [1e16, 1.0, -1e16] = 1.0 | RULINGS Q14c |
| AG-SUM-ONE-ENTITY | two equal-valued assertions of one attribute on one entity are one value with two supports and one binding row: SUM 10 + 10 on one entity is 10 and COUNT is 1; equal values on distinct entities each count | SUM(:conf/amount) with 10 asserted twice on entity agg:c = 10; COUNT with the same fixture = 1; SUM with 10 on agg:a and 10 on agg:b = 20 | RULINGS Q21 AMB-09 (provisional, flagged for Sam); PLAN C5.1 |
| AG-INT-RESULT | integer aggregate and arithmetic results project as IntegerValue with canonical decimal text, never as a JavaScript number |  | RULINGS Q21 AMB-10 |
| AG-AVG-I | AVG over integers without explicit conversion: preflight E-INTEGER-AVG |  | RULINGS Q8b; compiler.ts:1397-1401 |
| AG-AVG-CONV | AVG(toNumber(integer)) and AVG(number): binary64 of the exact sum divided by the count, rounded once; the explicit conversion is spelled toNumber(?v) |  | RULINGS Q8b; Q21 AMB-11 |
| AG-COUNT | COUNT over a variable counts distinct flattened values of that variable (core), so two entities with value 10 count 1 while SUM counts 20 |  | testkit 'datalog aggregates preserve duplicate rows and define empty and distinct results' |
| AG-EMPTY-UNGROUPED | ungrouped aggregate over no rows returns one row: COUNT 0; SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX null |  | same testkit case |
| AG-EMPTY-GROUPED | grouped aggregate over no rows returns no rows; an empty group never appears |  | wiki/problems/native-correlation.md (grouped empty SUM produces no row) |
| AG-MINMAX-TIES | MIN/MAX return the extreme value; a witness query keeps every tied entity |  | wiki/problems/native-correlation.md (tied integer-max winners) |
| AG-PACKET-COALESCE | packet tasks that state COALESCE(sum, 0) return 0 for an empty input; this is task-specific and recorded in the task recipe |  | packet workload 06 empty-currency |

### 4.5 Cardinality-many order

set semantics: equal values collapse to one element; elements ordered first by type family, then by value. Family order: boolean, integer, number, decimal, datetime, string, ref, json, blob. boolean: false < true; integer: numeric; number: numeric IEEE (-0.0 and +0.0 collapse, CMP-NEGZERO); decimal: exact numeric value (1.50 and 1.5 are one value); datetime: instant; string: Unicode codepoint sequence; ref: codepoint sequence of the target id; json: codepoint sequence of the canonical JSON text; blob: codepoint sequence of the content id. Family order per RULINGS Q14a and Q18: decimal is its own family between number and datetime; inside it, values sort by exact numeric value.

| Id | Rule | Source |

| CN-NEW-OR-WORSENED | with enforcement on, a command is rejected only when its post-state creates a new violation or worsens an existing one at some represented valid-time boundary; a pre-existing violation does not block an unrelated command and stays readable | packages/core/src/Constraint.ts:376 (newlyViolated) |
| CN-CARD-COUNT | write-time cardinality counts live assertions, including equal-valued duplicates (unchanged) | Constraint.ts:193; PLAN C5.1 |
| CN-PREEXISTING-CONFLICT | a card-one conflict that predates the enforcing write stays a conflict (C5.2) and reads per C5.3 | PLAN C5.2 |

### 4.7 Errors (O-ERR)

An expected error matches when the observed error's _tag equals the pinned tag and its reason equals the pinned reason (or one of the listed alternatives for multi-reason ids, the case names which), the original cause is retained, and no rows are returned. Any other error, a success, or partial rows is a FAIL.

### 5.3 Selector semantics

An obligation's cases are a list of {set, select}. select is a list of tags or named required case ids; 'all' selects every case of the set. The evaluator resolves the selection against the set's pinned manifest (lab/acceptance/cases/<set>.json, sha256 pinned in the contract version): the selected cases are those carrying any listed tag, plus any named case listed by id. The resolution must be non-empty, every listed entry must be in the set's requiredTags or requiredCases, and every requiredCases id must exist in the manifest. A set whose manifest is not pinned in the contract version cannot close any obligation. Declared executions = selected cases x modes (x 1 per receipt scope key); see MODE_RULE.

### 5.5 Validity classes

**VC** (calibration evidence; depends on nothing).
- VC1 runKind = calibration; create-only; its timestamp precedes every acceptance receipt that cites it
- VC2 binds the control profile identity and the load-contract or threshold registry hash
- VC3 every value is the registry value or tighter, or UNATTAINABLE with its retained measurement
- VC4 every ladder step's raw objects are retained
- VC5 preconditions that are acceptance obligations (for the NS calibration: S.population.year-one for the engine) are evaluated by the VA rules on the control profile; they never depend on VC records

**VA** (primary acceptance evidence; depends on VC).
- VA1 produced by lab/bin in this repository, append-only, every evidence object present under runs/objects with matching sha256
- VA2 profile identity complete and equal to the candidate profile
- VA3 build first: imported dist hashes produced in this run
- VA4 engine image digest equals the pin or a repaired image declared in this contract version
- VA5 endpoint contacted equals the slot's; never 15442, 17019 or a homebase host
- VA6 contract transitive hash, obligation definition hash, oracle files and case manifests equal the pinned values; every oracle used is ACCEPTED
- VA7 fixture content hash and a fresh scope recorded
- VA8 executed set equals the resolved selection x modes; skipped, unsupported, not-implemented all 0
- VA9 language trace pure for lane receipts; host steps only HS-NORMALIZE and HS-FRONTIER
- VA10 resource admission recorded; not BLOCKED_CAPACITY
- VA11 every threshold used is the registry value or comes from a VC-valid calibration record cited in calibrationRefs
- VA12 no failed acceptance receipt exists for the same obligation, scope key and profile; first failures retained
- VA13 named DIAGNOSTICS executed and retained
- VA14 composition bound: the four assignments with image digest, configuration hash and slot each, every replication edge, and the serving index's watermark at every read; engine-scope keys derived from the assignment (RULINGS Q28)
- VA15 for NS and GS receipts: the trace generator source hash and seed equal the frozen pair of load-contract.json; background and overlay commands accounted separately; the driver-recorded requested basis present for every read
- VA16 the profile is not a screening profile (SCREENING_PROFILES)

**VM** (mutation evidence; depends on VA).
- VM1 runKind = mutation; profile identity equals a VA-valid acceptance receipt's except the patch; oracle, case and gate hashes identical
- VM2 the patch touches only system-under-test files and is retained
- VM3 reach: the mutant's reach probe fired at least once inside a targeted case
- VM4 kill: at least one targeted case failed by a comparator mismatch on an identified assertion; errors, timeouts, crashes and setup failures do not count

**VV** (verifier evidence; depends on VA).
- VV1 runKind = verifier; agentId not among authorsOfCodeUnderTest of the verified receipts
- VV2 same profile identity as the verified receipts
- VV3 coverage per the obligation's verifier mode (VERIFIER_MODES)
- VV4 the verifier's own evaluator recomputes every verdict from retained objects; any mismatch fails the obligation

### 5.6 Closure rules

| Rule | Evidence | Validity | Recomputed from retained evidence | Holds when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CR-PASS-ALL | case-result | VA | each case verdict = comparator(oracle expected, retained raw result bytes) | every resolved case passes in every declared mode |
| CR-COUNTEREXAMPLE | case-result | VA | as CR-PASS-ALL, with the original oracle file whose hash is unchanged since the first recorded failure | every original counterexample passes with unedited case text |
| CR-MUTANT-KILL | mutation-record, case-result | VM, VA | reach hits from the retained probe log; killing assertions re-compared from retained expected and observed objects | every listed mutant meets MUTANT_RULE and the clean receipt passes |
| CR-OBSERVE | observation | VA | O-OBS verdict per protocol from retained samples and events | every required protocol verdict is PASS within the obligation's thresholds |
| CR-FAULT | fault-witness, case-result | VA | expected outcome chosen from the last witnessed transition in COMMIT_OUTCOMES (or the case's declared outcome), compared with final state, caller outcome, retries and post-recovery case results | every fault point injected at least T-FAULT-REPS times and every injection matches |
| CR-STATIC | static-witness | VA | CMP-DIAGNOSTICS on retained tsc output; any-scan re-run | observed diagnostics equal expected exactly and the any-scan is empty |
| CR-SCALE | scale-dataset, case-result, observation | VA | population counts versus O-REPLAY analytic counts; sample verdicts by comparator; capacity verdict by OBS-RESOURCE | counts equal, every sample passes, run admitted and within envelope |
| CR-PERF | case-result, observation, plan-record | VA, VC | latency and ratio statistics from retained timings | every named threshold met in each of 3 independent runs |
| CR-METRICS | observation | VA | metric values from retained samples; secondary thresholds reported against their values (SECONDARY_RULE) | every listed metric and every named secondary threshold present and measured; a secondary value never fails the rule |
| CR-NS | ns-run | VA, VC | every named NS bar from retained raw events under TARGETS 1.1: goodput counts only reads whose answer equals the oracle at the driver-recorded requested basis; latencies from the scheduled offer to the published ACK; ratios against the same run's matched-phase baselines; per-core throughput from the receipt's CPU quota; affected-subject sets against O-REPLAY plus O-DOMAIN | every named bar met in each of T-RUNS independent runs, on the frozen trace generator and seed of load-contract.json, with a VC record for every named threshold; under PAIR_0 (RULINGS Q60, provisional) a comparative bar holds only from paired rounds (8 to 24, pooled-quantile ratios with a bootstrap over rounds, the PAIR_0 margins), an absolute bar only from GREEN windows (an unjudged bar is never met), latency histograms count every offered command at its censor time, and arms under different slot regimes are never compared |
| CR-GS | ns-run, case-result, fault-witness | VA, VC | only evidence whose ns-run measurement equals the obligation's params.scenario counts; scenario correctness from retained answers against O-REPLAY (state), O-DOMAIN (domain outputs under WORLD_W0) or O-HAND; positive and negative witnesses; every named failure schedule's expected outcome; commit and feed integrity from retained receipts and feed entries; every named bar from retained raw events | zero wrong answers, zero lost or duplicated commits, zero feed gaps or order violations, every witness and failure-schedule outcome as expected, every named bar met, in each of T-RUNS runs, on every compared composition |
| CR-REQUIREMENT | requirement-route, case-result | VA | each test verdict from retained results; the route record checked for a plain statement when WORKAROUND | the engine declares NATIVE or a documented WORKAROUND and every test of the requirement passes on that route; an OPEN requirement never excludes the engine from comparison |
| CR-CALIBRATION | calibration-record | VC | the required set is the union of the thresholds named by every NS obligation (obligations.json NS.calibration params.requiredThresholds); VC3 check of each value against the registry | the required set is non-empty and a VC-valid record holds a value for every member; an empty set or a missing member fails closed (RULINGS Q26) |
| CR-MATRIX | case-result | VA | matrix cells from obligations.json capabilityMatrix and the cited receipts | every required cell EXACT with a receipt; every raw-required KNOWN-LIMIT cell has its exception record and guide entry |
| CR-PROVENANCE | provenance-manifest | VA | manifest inputs compared with the guide and docs hashes | inputs are only the raw-query guide and engine public docs; the author is a fresh agent |
| CR-WITNESS | observation, case-result | VA | OBS-WORK work-unit ratios from retained engine-side counters | every named witness threshold met and answers equal the no-reuse or fresh-recompute run |
| CR-W0-COVERAGE | w0-coverage-record | VA | O-DOMAIN evaluates R1 and R2 over the frozen trace generator and seed at each rung and recomputes every W0-* statistic | every W0-* floor met and every W0_PIN field non-null and equal to the reviewed files' sha256; a null pin fails closed (RULINGS Q31i) |
| CR-BUDGET | budget-record, observation | VA | complete-path cost and NS measurements from retained evidence against budgets.json | within the absolute bars and caps and within the A0-relative allowances at every rung, compared cumulatively against the frozen A0 control |

### 5.7 Applicability, carry-forward and fresh final acceptance

- Bound identities: imported source files; imported dist files; engine image digest; engine configuration; resource caps; fixture contents; enabled capabilities; gate script versions; oracle file versions; case manifests; acceptance-rule version (contract transitive hash and obligation definition hash).
- A receipt carries forward to a later profile only when every bound identity is unchanged, checked by an explicit applicability record (AP) that recomputes each identity on the later profile. Carry-forward serves intermediate tracking only.
- A receipt made on a screening profile (SCREENING_PROFILES, RULINGS Q16) is evidence for candidate comparison only: it never passes VA, never closes an obligation, never feeds calibration and never carries forward.

- The final acceptance of the selected integrated profile is entirely fresh: every obligation, including scale rungs and load levels, runs on that profile; nothing carries into it.

### 5.8 Verifier coverage

| Mode | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| rerun | The verifier reruns the obligation's full selection on the same profile and recomputes every verdict from retained objects. |
| re-evaluate-and-spot | The verifier independently re-evaluates every retained answer byte, fault outcome and coverage record for every ladder level, scenario, rung and run, and performs at least one spot rerun per profile unit (one per lane and NS measurement; one per lane and golden scenario; one per lane and rung). |

Every obligation's verifier mode is listed with it in section 10.

### 5.9 Mutation controls

A mutant counts only when (1) its reach probe fired at least once during a targeted case, and (2) at least one targeted case failed through a comparator mismatch on an identified assertion (case id and assertion id), not through an error, timeout, crash or setup failure. Mutants patch only the system under test; oracle, case and gate hashes are identical to the clean receipt.

Oracle lifecycle: TO-BUILD or TO-AUTHOR, then BUILT, then ACCEPTED after independent review recorded in the commit; only ACCEPTED oracles with pinned file hashes close obligations (VA6). Comparators:

| Comparator | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| CMP-SET-ROWS | sorted unique canonical rows equal (packet runner semantics: runner.ts:900-912) |
| CMP-BAG-ROWS | multisets of canonical rows equal |
| CMP-ORDERED-ROWS | sequences of canonical rows equal, order included |
| CMP-EXACT-VALUE | typed values equal: integers exactly, decimals by exact value and declared scale, binary64 bit patterns (sign of zero included), text codepoints, datetime instants, json canonical text plus original key order where the case says so |
| CMP-ERROR | An expected error matches when the observed error's _tag equals the pinned tag and its reason equals the pinned reason (or one of the listed alternatives for multi-reason ids, the case names which), the original cause is retained, and no rows are returned. Any other error, a success, or partial rows is a FAIL. |
| CMP-PAGES | the page sequence equals the expected sequence: same rows per page, no duplicate or skipped row, same returned basis on every page |
| CMP-DIAGNOSTICS | the set of {file, line, column, code} diagnostics equals the expected set exactly |

### 6.1 O-REPLAY (independent Python event replay)

- **Inputs.** The captured command intent (ordered submissions with operations, typed values in canonical encoding, entity ids and types, valid intervals, preconditions, meta, enforcement mode and rules, nested-transaction structure), schema releases, and durable-decision evidence (engine commit evidence or the log of record read back, and the fault witness). ACK receipts bind only generated identities: assertion ids, txIds and recorded instants.
- **Clocks.** Recorded instants are not assumed monotonic in position order; separate runtimes supply their own clocks (PLAN C1). Histories with equal and with decreasing recorded instants are first-class cases (EV-SAME-R, EV-DECREASING-R, CS-TEMPORAL decreasing-clock).
- **R independent of P.** A cut is (scope, P, optional R, V). Recorded visibility is `recordedPosition <= P` and, when R is bound, `recordedAt <= R`, evaluated independently: an assertion with a later position but an earlier instant is invisible at P below its position, and an assertion at a lower position with an instant above R is invisible at R.
- **Position accounting.** Positions are totally ordered coordinates (POSITION: (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal), lexicographic, not necessarily dense; RULINGS Q31c): the oracle sorts committed transacts by coordinate and assigns its own dense ordinals for cuts; nested transacts inside one engine transaction share one offset and take consecutive ordinals in callback order; aborted offsets are accounted from the feed's resolution stream; the oracle checks every receipt coordinate against the committed order and fails the run on a mismatch.
- **Outcomes.** The oracle derives each command's expected outcome from intent, order, preconditions, enforcement (CN-NEW-OR-WORSENED) and durable-decision evidence (COMMIT_OUTCOMES), then compares the receipts' outcomes afterwards. A receipt never decides which command is valid or committed.
- **Outputs.** Complete assertion metadata; raw-lifetime and as-of snapshot history; entity models (card-one value or E-CONFLICTING-VALUES per C5; card-many per CARD_MANY_ORDER; absent optional as a missing property; includes at the same basis; timelines); transaction records with ordered changes and the logical journal facts (C6); cursor page sequences; support counts; C1 eligibility routes (for O-PLAN); arithmetic, comparison and aggregate results per section 4; analytic scale counts per population stratum (SCALE_POPULATION, section S).
- **Independence.** Python stdlib only; imports no repository code; its own exact integers and decimals, IEEE binary64 (via struct) and codepoint ordering; no casefolding.
- **Self-checks before ACCEPTED.** Reproduce O-HAM finite-nine, O-CFG8 tiny-v4 and the O-EVT cut semantics where domains overlap; unit tests for every table row of section 4.

### 6.2 O-SHAPE

Each case file entry carries: resultSemantics: set | bag | ordered; groupingKey: list of variables with COMPARISON_RULES identity; unboundHandling: exclude-row | null-cell (stated per projected variable); comparator: CMP-SET-ROWS | CMP-BAG-ROWS | CMP-ORDERED-ROWS; expectedRows; citation (SPARQL 1.1 or SQL section, or the packet task).

- Packet-derived shapes use set semantics (runner sorted-unique comparison).
- Negation controls compare the projected entity set.
- Aggregate controls follow AGGREGATE_RULES; empty groups per AG-EMPTY-*.
- Tied extremes keep every witness row (AG-MINMAX-TIES).
- An unbound projected variable is a null cell only where the case says null-cell; otherwise the row is excluded.

### 6.3 O-OBS protocols

| Protocol | Evidence fields | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OBS-CANCEL | requestId, connectionId, tCancelRequested, tCallerSettled, callerError, transportAck {kind, t}, engineActiveSamples [{t, activeQueryIds}], tDrained, reuseQueryId, tReuseOk | PASS iff callerError matches E-CANCELLED or E-TIMEOUT as the case pins, transportAck observed, the request id absent from every engine sample after tDrained with tDrained - tCancelRequested <= T-DRAIN-MS, sample gaps <= 1000 ms over [tCancelRequested, tDrained + 5000 ms], and the reuse query on the same connection succeeds |
| OBS-PREABORT | requestId, engineStatementLog [{t, tag}], coverage | PASS iff zero engine statements carry the request id over the full coverage window |
| OBS-CONNECTIONS | poolDeclarations [{label, max}], engineConnectionSamples [{t, label, count}], baseline, tClose | PASS iff every sample <= declared max and the count equals baseline within T-CONN-RELEASE-MS after tClose |
| OBS-SCRATCH | relation, countBefore, countAfter, resolutionReceipts | PASS iff countAfter = countBefore for every scratch relation and every unknown working outcome is resolved |
| OBS-NO-MUTATION | engineMutationCounterBefore, engineMutationCounterAfter, counterSource | PASS iff the engine's committed-transaction or update counter is unchanged across the read |
| OBS-RESOURCE | forecast {memory, disk}, peaks [{owner, rss, disk, t}], envelope | PASS iff every peak <= forecast <= envelope (and <= T-PLANNER-MEM-BYTES where named) |
| OBS-AVAILABILITY | tFailure, probes [{t, kind: write\|read, outcome}] | PASS iff a write and a read both succeed at some t <= tFailure + T-AVAIL-WINDOW-MS with no manual restart event |
| OBS-SCALE-COUNT | population, countQueryCaseResult, analyticCount | PASS iff the count query's answer equals O-REPLAY's analytic count |
| OBS-WORK | operation, engineWorkUnits {rowsScanned, rowsWritten, triplesTouched, bytesWritten}, source | ratio of work units between the compared operations, evaluated against the named witness threshold |
| OBS-MAINTENANCE | kind, tStart, tEnd, lagSamples | events present; lag statistics against the named threshold |
| OBS-ERASURE-SCAN | inventoryEntry, location, scanMethod, plaintextHits, derivedChannelHits, keyDestroyedEvidence, tScan | PASS iff every PROTECTED_COPY_INVENTORY location of the lane is scanned after the erasure published and shows zero plaintext and zero derived-channel hits, or every surviving copy there is shown to be encrypted only under the destroyed per-subject key (key exclusivity, RULINGS Q31f) |
| OBS-WATERMARK | readId, basisPosition, servingIndex, watermarkAtRead, waitMs, route, fallbackIndex | PASS iff no read was answered by an index that was not eligible (COMPOSITION eligibility: watermark in the basis epoch, C1, reconstructability, erasure frontier), every wait before routing is within T-WATERMARK-WAIT-MS, every route and its surface language is recorded, and the fallback latency is inside the read's measured latency |
| OBS-ACK-ORDER | commitPosition, tSourcePublished, tAck, ackSender, ryowPullRoute | PASS iff the source of truth sent every ACK, tAck >= tSourcePublished for every commit, and every pull at a returned position was served by an eligible index or the fallback |
| OBS-FAULT-TRANSITIONS | transition, t, durableEvidenceObject | the last witnessed transition is the last one whose durable evidence is present after the crash |

### 6.4 O-PLAN protocols

| Protocol | Evidence fields | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OBS-PLAN-ROUTE | queryId, route: projection \| exact, eligibilityInputs {scopeOwner, mappingGeneration, recordedTimeBound, positionKind, validInstant, markerState, partialOrConflictedReferenced} | PASS iff route equals O-REPLAY's C1 model: projection only when every C1 condition holds for the whole query |
| OBS-PLAN-ACCESS | queryId, enginePlanObject, accessPathClass | key-bounded iff the XTDB plan uses an _id IID selector (scan.clj selector) for the probed table, or the QLever plan's first operation is an index scan with the subject or predicate-object bound; otherwise scan |
| OBS-PLAN-COST | queryId, declaredBudget, estimate, actual | PASS iff actual <= declaredBudget, or the query stopped with the pinned error at the budget |

### 6.5 O-SPEC rules

- Positive witnesses assert exact types with an Equals<A, B> helper; assignability alone does not count.
- Every asserted type is also checked not to be any (IsAny<T> is false); an accidental any fails.
- Negative witnesses do not use @ts-expect-error; tsc runs on the witness set and the observed set of {file, line, column, code} must equal the pinned expected set exactly (CMP-DIAGNOSTICS); an unrelated diagnostic fails.
- The emitted public declarations are scanned: no exported symbol resolves to any except an explicitly listed allowlist in the witness manifest.
- Witnesses import only from packed public package exports, compiled with the consumer's strict tsconfig.
