### 7.1 Value types (CS-TYPES8, CS-TYPES8-NEG, CS-WIDEN)

| Family | Edge values |
| --- | --- |
| string | "", ASCII mixed case A E c z, NFC U+00E9 and NFD e U+0301 as distinct values, U+E000, U+10000, U+1F600, quote, backslash, CR, LF, a 64 KiB text |
| integer | 0, 1, -1, 2^53-1, -(2^53-1) on every lane; 2^53+1, 2^59-1, -2^59 where the lane accepts them; values beyond the lane's range belong to CS-RANGE-OUT |
| decimal | 0.00, 16.50, 16.49, a 38-digit value, a negative value, the TDK1 key and canonical text round trip (CS-DECIMAL covers scale overflow) |
| number (binary64, approximate values only) | +0.0, -0.0, 0.1, 0.30000000000000004, 1.0000000000000002, 2^53 as a double, 5e-324, 2.2250738585072014e-308, 1.7976931348623157e308, -1.5, 3.0 (stays a number) |
| boolean | true, false |
| datetime | 0, a negative instant, 1700000000000.5 (fractional millisecond), the earliest and latest instant Triplex accepts |
| ref | same type, another type, an entity created in the same command |
| json | {"b":1,"a":2} (key order kept), nested arrays and objects, non-ASCII text, 1e300 |
| blob | descriptor with and without filename, size 0, a size above 2^32 |

CS-TYPES8-NEG (each rejected atomically): lone surrogate, NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity, non-canonical integer text ("01", "+1", "1.0", "-0"), integer outside the core integer type, invalid datetime, unparseable json, blob descriptor with a negative size.

CS-WIDEN: integer 9007199254740993 first (lanes that accept it), then in the same attribute or physical column a whole-number float, a text value through an untyped attribute, and for QLever an invalid typed literal through the raw wire; re-read the first value everywhere.

### 7.2 Numbers (CS-NUMERIC) and errors (CS-ERRORS)

Every example in sections 4.1 to 4.4 is a CS-NUMERIC case with that expected answer. CS-ERRORS has one case per ERROR_TABLE entry reachable from a read surface.

### 7.3 Fault points (CS-FAULT)

The expected outcome after a fault is chosen from the last transition with durable or engine-side evidence observed by the fault injector after the crash (the log file's records read back, the engine's committed transactions, the publication marker), never from the system's own claim. A transition the protocol declares but the receipt does not witness fails the case.

every composition declares its source implementation and protocol variant (RULINGS Q55b): log-source (a host log or broker is the source of truth and an engine is its replica: the QLever lane's broker (C2), EXP-P2Q's host log, and XTDB behind the host log in EXP-P2B) or engine-source (the engine is the source: XTDB's native commit path); each variant has its own witnessed transition table and the composition's declared variant selects it.

**log-source transitions.**

| Transition | Witness evidence |
| --- | --- |
| QT0-RECEIVED | broker request log entry |
| QT1-VALIDATED | group member accepted against staged state (broker trace) |
| QT2-LOGGED | COMMIT record present in the log file after restart (fsync completed); this is the irrevocable decision |
| QT3-APPLY-SENT | update operation sent (broker trace) |
| QT4s-SOURCE-PUBLISHED | the source's decision is durable under its declared durability configuration and the source's own read surface (the broker's log reader or overlay) answers at the group's P; it may precede QT3 (RULINGS Q55b) |
| QT4r-REPLICA-APPLIED | the replica's publication marker for the group's P is visible in a query against the replica (RULINGS Q55b) |
| QT5-VERIFIED | complete expected effects and absences checked (broker trace and independent query through three access paths) |
| QT6-ACKED | caller received the success receipt |

**log-source expected outcomes.**

| Fault after | Final state | Original caller | Retry with the same commandId | Reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| QT0-RECEIVED or QT1-VALIDATED (no QT2 evidence) | the command is absent unless a later attempt commits it; it is never committed twice | typed failure or E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN; never success | evaluated as a fresh command (commits at most once in total) | - |
| QT2-LOGGED (no QT4s evidence) | the group MUST be published by recovery with the position decided at QT2; it can never become absent | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN or E-COMMIT-PENDING; never success before source publication (QT4s) | before publication: E-COMMIT-PENDING or E-REPAIRING; after publication: the original success receipt (same txId and position) | never show the group before publication; E-REPAIRING while fenced |
| QT3-APPLY-SENT (no QT4s evidence) | as QT2-LOGGED; partial permutation state must not be served: the lane fences and recovery re-applies or rebuilds | as QT2-LOGGED | as QT2-LOGGED | E-REPAIRING while fenced; after recovery all access paths agree |
| QT4s-SOURCE-PUBLISHED (no QT4r evidence) | published at the source; the replica catches up from the log and recovery never makes the group absent | success (the ACK may follow QT4s, RULINGS Q31e, Q55b) or E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN | the original success receipt | repository pulls see the group by routing (replica, else overlay, else the source's log); native reads follow COMPOSITION readGuarantees; a replica behind the source is not a failure |
| QT4r-REPLICA-APPLIED (no QT5 evidence) | published at the source and the replica; recovery completes verification before any new write | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN or success | the original success receipt | show the group; E-REPAIRING while fenced |
| QT5-VERIFIED failure (verification mismatch) | lane fenced; recovery republishes the logged state; final state equals O-REPLAY with the group present | no success until recovery establishes publication | E-REPAIRING until recovered, then the original success receipt | E-REPAIRING while fenced |
| QT5-VERIFIED (no QT6 evidence): lost ACK | published | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN | the original success receipt | show the group |

A success receipt is valid only if its timestamp is after the group's QT4s-SOURCE-PUBLISHED evidence; a repository pull by the same client issued after the success receipt sees the group by routing, whether or not QT4r has been reached (read-your-writes, COMPOSITION readGuarantees).

**engine-source transitions.**

| Transition | Witness evidence |
| --- | --- |
| XT0-RECEIVED | client trace |
| XT1-BEGIN-SENT | driver trace |
| XT2-ENGINE-COMMITTED | the transaction is committed in the engine after restart (operation marker row present at its position) |
| XT3-ACKED | caller received the success receipt |

**engine-source expected outcomes.**

| Fault after | Final state | Original caller | Retry with the same commandId | Reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| XT0 or XT1 (no XT2 evidence) | absent unless a later attempt commits it; never committed twice | typed failure or E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN; never success | evaluated as a fresh command | - |
| XT2-ENGINE-COMMITTED (no XT3 evidence): lost ACK | present exactly once at its position | E-OUTCOME-UNKNOWN; resolution through EP-RESOLVE returns committed | E-COMMAND-COMMITTED carrying the original txId (or the original receipt) | show the transaction (publication is atomic with commit) |

A success receipt is valid only after XT2 evidence; read-your-writes holds for the same client.

Access paths verified after each fault: XTDB `_id` lookup and column-predicate scan; QLever subject, predicate-object and object scans; plus the repository, the native surface in every language of the engine and the raw recipe.

### 7.4 Entity suite (CS-ENTITY)

- Schema: at least three EntityTypes using all eight families, cardinality one and many, required, optional, unique, a ref with target type and a reverse ref; two releases (v2 adds an optional attribute and a constraint).
- Command stream: create; correction; card-many add and remove; future validTo crossing later; retraction; with enforcement off, equal duplicates (one value, two supports) and distinct-value conflicts and overlapping intervals; presence toggles (convention until the Q9 policy); two commits sharing one recorded instant; a second runtime with a lagging clock; one nested transaction with two positions; the v2 release.
- Cut catalog: every phase position, recorded instants between and at commits (including the decreasing one), valid instants at, before and after every boundary; frozen from the oracle's derived positions, checked against receipts.
- Operations at each cut: get; getMany with missing ids; find with equality, range, membership and ref predicates per family, include, order, limit and cursor continuation; timeline; at(basis) for current, past R, past V and both. Conflicts expect E-CONFLICTING-VALUES per C5.
- Modes: current, reopen, engine restart. Size: a hand-built core of at most 200 entities plus a seeded generated variant.

### 7.5 Raw recipes (CS-RAW-RECIPES, CS-RAW-MAPPED)

The raw-query guide documents physical names, scope selection, how to express current, as-of position, recorded-time and valid-instant reads, the conflict indicator and values(attribute), every exact channel, every mapped recipe (RG-* entries of `capability-matrix.md`) and every known limit. Query classes: RP-POINT, RP-RANGE, RP-ORDER-PAGE, RP-CROSS-FAMILY, RP-JOIN, RP-ANTIJOIN, RP-AGGREGATE, RP-BASIS, RP-DATASET, RP-HISTORY, RP-INTERVAL, RP-JOURNAL.

### 7.6 Cursor and basis continuation (CS-CURSOR)

A cursor or a requested historical basis issued before any transition below continues successfully afterward (through the exact ledger path where the projection changed), returning exactly the rows O-REPLAY computes at the cursor's basis. An available retained cut never becomes unavailable because its projection, mapping or index changed. No retention policy exists, so 'cut no longer retained' is never a permitted outcome.

| Must continue | Transition |
| --- | --- |
| CT-ENGINE-RESTART | engine restart |
| CT-CLIENT-REOPEN | fresh runtime and client on the same scope |
| CT-RELEASE-CHANGE | a new schema release is published; the cursor continues under its own release's mapping |
| CT-PROJECTION-REBUILD | projection rebuilt or backfilled |
| CT-GENERATION-SWITCH | projection or index generation switch |
| CT-PUBLICATION-ADVANCE | newer commits published after the cursor's P |
| CT-MAINTAINING | QLever marker in MAINTAINING |
| CT-BOUNDARY-PASS | a valid-time boundary passes after the cursor was issued |
| CT-COMPACTION | XTDB compaction or GC, QLever rebuild-index or checkpoint |
| CT-BROKER-FAILOVER | broker replaced and recovery completed |
| CT-BACKUP-RESTORE | restore into a fresh engine from a backup taken after the cursor was issued |
| CT-FENCE-RECOVERED | lane fenced, then recovered: during the fence E-REPAIRING is permitted; after recovery the same cursor must continue |

| Permitted error case | Error | Reason | Only when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CE-MALFORMED | E-CURSOR | malformed | the token was altered or is not a token |
| CE-OTHER-SCOPE | E-CURSOR | other-scope | the cursor belongs to another scope |
| CE-OTHER-QUERY | E-CURSOR | other-query | the cursor belongs to a query with a different definition hash |
| CE-FUTURE-BASIS | E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE | basis-not-reached | the requested position is beyond the latest published position (RULINGS Q72f: E-UNAVAILABLE-CUT retired) |
| CE-FENCED | E-REPAIRING | repairing | only while the lane is fenced; the case also asserts continuation after recovery |

## 8. North-star workload, golden scenarios, year-one population and budgets

### 8.1 Fixed writer trace (TARGETS section 2)

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Command shape | 5 to 10 facts: 0.6; 11 to 25 facts: 0.3; 26 to 50 facts: 0.1; one subject per command; blob reference for documents |
| Writers | people 0.4 (evidence, decisions); systems 0.3 (signals, often duplicated); agents 0.1 (proposals); runtime 0.2 (action outcomes) |
| Rate | steady 15 facts/s; bursts 750 facts/s for 60 s every 600 s |
| Duplicates | 0.1 of system signals re-sent with the same commandId |
| Lost ACKs | 0.01 of commands, retried |
| Corrections | 0.01 of commands, valid time 30 days back |
| Reads per write | 10 to 100: each command triggers a reconcile pull at the returned tx, dependency lookups, projection updates and UI refreshes |
| Conflicts | optimistic compare-and-set on the subject's last position; serial per subject, parallel across subjects |
| Bulk lane | separate and throttled; used only by the bulk measurements |
| Seed | a recorded seed fixes the whole trace; the same seed gives the same bytes |

The P1 reader ladder, the P2 to P4 probes, the P5 sweep and the secondary measurements are in `load-contract.json`.

### 8.2 Golden scenario rules (TARGETS section 6)

- A seeded, deterministic generator produces the command stream and the reads; the same seed gives the same bytes.
- Expected answers come from the independent oracles, never from a system under test: O-REPLAY for database state and values, O-DOMAIN for domain outputs and effects under WORLD_W0, or a frozen hand derivation with a citation (O-HAND).
- A scenario's commands are overlaid on the background trace, never instead of it; the receipt accounts for both streams separately.
- Every scenario carries positive witnesses (subjects that must change, GS-nn-WITNESS-POS) and negative witnesses (subjects that must not, GS-nn-WITNESS-NEG).
- Plan-impact preview (GS.11) and activation (GS.10) are compared at one common input basis (GS-10-11-COMMON-BASIS).
- The added failure schedules of GS_FAILURE_SCHEDULES (TARGETS 6.1) are named cases of their scenario and must meet their expected outcome.
- Each GS obligation binds only its own scenario: it selects its own tag and named cases, names exactly its own bars plus T-RUNS, and its receipt carries an ns-run whose measurement is its own scenario id (RULINGS Q26).
- Unless a scenario says otherwise it runs on P-YEAR-ONE with the fixed writer trace running and 256 concurrent pinned readers (P-NS).
- A scenario fails on any wrong answer, any lost or duplicated commit, any feed gap or order violation, or any missed bar; its receipt records the correctness verdicts and the P1 to P5 measurements together.
- All 20 run on every composition being compared, and the final acceptance reruns all 20 fresh.
- Numbers inside the scenarios: pay rates, hours and money use integer cents (the integer kind) or the decimal kind (TDK1 key); the scenarios include the range rules 'pay rate at or above 16.50' and 'hours over 40' (cases GS-NUM-RANGE-1650 and GS-NUM-HOURS-40, selected by GS.18's dashboard filters) and at least one write of a value the lane cannot hold, which must fail with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE, E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW or E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (GS-NUM-UNHOLDABLE, selected by GS.02).
- Every GS stream is W0-valid and every domain claim a scenario names is checked by O-DOMAIN; a scenario whose spec names a domain claim and whose run makes no such check fails closed. The W01 world vocabulary is retired
- The GS background is the frozen TARGETS 2.1 trace through the W0 trace mapper (Q92k); the private writerTrace is retired; every measured window holds one burst and one maintenance event
- GS world admission follows Q93a: a G0 content fingerprint per run; a fresh scope or verified clone per run; store counts at start and end; on lane Q the Q91a counts
- Every GS receipt before contract 0.4.0 is DIAGNOSTIC: none closes an obligation or enters a comparison. The GS.12 defect and the W01b harness findings stay as defect reports
- GS.04b applies only to compositions with a separate current store; on those it is required. GS.04's engine-kill schedule is required on every lane and runs only on an exclusive slot
- GS.19's outbox and GS.10's publications must be the product's atomic outbox; a harness-side outbox file can pass only GS.19's P3 checks, as a diagnostic
- GS.10's race (in-flight reconciles finish on the old release) is scheduled as EXP-P5 round C, right after rounds A and B, and is required for GS.10 to close
- GS.03's vendor-revision rule goes into W0-1.2 with an O-DOMAIN `signal-ack` operation; the `superseded` outcome stays flagged for Sam

### 8.3 Year-one measurement population

Role: measurement size for P1 to P5 and the golden scenarios; not a target in itself (lab/SCOPE.md section 2 item 2). Source: lab/TARGETS.md section 2 (year-one scale; rungs 10k, 100k, 1m, 10m) and section 1 P4 (history depths 1, 3, 10); qualification/benchmark-contract.json (topologies, query families); acceptance review r1 finding 13. Rungs: 10000, 100000, 1000000, 10000000; every count and stratum scales proportionally with the rung; hub in-degree is 1% of the rung's entities; shares are identical at every rung. At year one: {"entities": 10000000, "activeDomainFacts": 100000000, "retainedFactsMin": 150000000, "retainedFactsNote": "TARGETS section 2: retained history 150M to 500M facts per year; the history strata below give about 162M retained facts"}. Facts per entity: 10 active domain facts: label (string), risk score (number, approximate), pay rate (decimal, scale 2), hours (integer), headcount (integer), flag (boolean), group (ref), category (string, skewed), start date (datetime), status changed at (datetime). Written through public writes (EP-WRITER, or EP-BULK for the initial load), every command ACKed with a receipt, no unresolved outcome.

| Stratum | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| TN-LARGE | one tenant with 1m entities |
| TN-SMALL | 1,000 tenants with 1k entities each |
| TN-REST | the remaining entities in one default tenant |
| H1 | 0.5: depth 1: no correction |
| H3 | 0.35: depth 3: two corrections on each of five attributes |
| H10 | 0.15: depth 10: nine corrections on each of two attributes |
| EV-PRESENCE | 1 entity per 1,000 toggles presence true -> false -> true |
| EV-RETRO | 1% of commands are valid-time corrections 30 days back (TARGETS section 2) |
| EV-VALID-FUTURE | 5% of entities hold a fact whose validTo falls inside the measurement window |
| EV-VALID-PAST | 5% of entities hold a fact already closed by valid time |
| EV-SAME-R | 1 command per 10,000 shares its recorded instant with the next command |
| EV-DECREASING-R | 1 command per 10,000 is written by a second runtime whose clock is behind |
| EV-NESTED | 1 command per 10,000 is a nested transaction holding two positions |
| EV-UNHOLDABLE | write attempts of values a lane cannot hold (integers beyond its declared range, decimals beyond scale) appear in the stream and must fail typed |
| TP-CHAIN | 1,000 chains of depth 50 (at 10m; proportional below) |
| TP-TREE | 1,000 trees, fanout 4, depth 6 |
| TP-DIAMOND | 10,000 diamonds |
| TP-CYCLE | 1,000 cycles of length 3 to 20 |
| TP-FANOUT | 10 hubs, each with incoming refs from 1% of entities |
| TP-SKEW | category Zipf s = 1.1 over 1,000 values; flag about 50% true |
| TP-PULL | every subject's pull subgraph spans 3 to 6 hops and 50 to 2,000 facts (TARGETS P4) |
| RC-S | exactly 1 row |
| RC-M | 100 to 1,000 rows |
| RC-L | at least 100,000 rows or the documented row limit (E-ROW-LIMIT beyond) |

Counted separately: entities per tenant, domain facts, structural facts, assertion versions and retirements, config facts, journal, claim, receipt and feed metadata, maintenance relations, engine rows or triples by physical role, edges, presence events, corrections.

Correctness: S.correctness.query-families runs per rung, at least T-SAMPLES-PER-FAMILY samples per family with at least T-SAMPLES-PER-STRATUM in every applicable stratum (history, topology, tenant, result cardinality), plus complete-count queries for every population; deterministic sample selection from the generator seed, never from query answers.

### 8.6 Budgets

Budgets are re-frozen after EXP-N02 measures the A0 controls, in a create-only budget-freeze receipt (A0 control measurements at every rung, this file's sha256), before any candidate is evaluated against them. No candidate comparison may cite a budget that has not been re-frozen. A hypothesis's predicted cost never sets its own allowance. Changing a budget creates a new profile version; loosening an NS bar needs Sam. A0 = the ledger-only baseline profile (status-quo adapters, no projection), measured on the same slot configuration, writer trace and rung. Where A0 cannot complete a rung, only the absolute bars and caps apply there and the failure is recorded. Every promotion and the final acceptance compare the integrated candidate with the frozen A0 control at the same rung, never with the previous promotion, so small regressions accumulate against one fixed reference. Every NS-* bar of obligations.json thresholds applies as an absolute budget at P-YEAR-ONE; resource caps: memory peak within the 11 GiB reservation pool, disk peak within the 50 GiB stop line of the 60 GiB VM (lab/PLAN.md section 8).

| Budget | Allowance vs A0 | Direction | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B-WRITE-BYTES-PER-FACT | 4.0 | max | provisional (RULINGS Q16): projection, indexes, journal and feed together |
| B-INGEST-FACTS-PER-S | 0.5 | min | provisional (RULINGS Q16) |
| B-CURRENT-PULL-P99 | 1.0 | max | derived: the current path must not be slower than ledger-only |
| B-COMMIT-P99 | 1.25 | max | derived from NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256 |
| B-MEMORY-PEAK | 1.5 | max | provisional (RULINGS Q16) |
| B-DISK-PEAK | 2.0 | max | provisional (RULINGS Q16) |

Components counted: ledger, projection, index tables, journal, log of record, mutation broker, verification, scratch work, fallback (exact path) reads, maintenance, clients.

### 8.7 Composition identity (TARGETS 4.1, RULINGS Q28)

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| assignments | source, current, history, analytics |
| engines | each assignment is XTDB, QLever or Datomic |
| engineIds | xtdb, qlever, datomic |
| receiptBinding | every receipt binds, per assignment, the engine image digest, configuration hash and slot; every replication edge (feed consumer source hash, translation generation); and each serving index's watermark at read time |
| basis | a basis is a source-of-truth position (POSITION coordinates (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal)) plus a valid time |
| eligibility | index I is eligible to serve basis B only when all hold: its watermark (a fully resolved prefix) has reached B in B's epoch; C1's eligibility for the query (mapping, valid time, exact cut); I can actually reconstruct B (a current-only index only when B is at or after the last change to every attribute the read touches, the validity interval of R18); and I has applied every erasure published so far, independently of B (ERASURE frontier) (RULINGS Q31d) |
| watermarkRouting | a read that finds no eligible index waits at most T-WATERMARK-WAIT-MS for one, then routes to an eligible fallback (the source of truth's own query surface or another index); the fallback's latency counts in the read's own latency; the receipt records the route and the surface language, a cross-language fallback is counted per surface, and fallbacks are reported as a share of reads per window; no index answers for a basis it is not eligible for (RULINGS Q31d) |
| fallbackEquivalence | outage read-your-own-write is tested on every serving surface the composition claims, native surfaces included, each against its readGuarantees guarantee (RULINGS Q55c); a stale fallback is rejected; where a fallback answers in another language, both recipes are bound to one semantic query identity (parameters, basis, meaning) and one expected answer from the oracle; total request latency and language attribution stay recorded (RULINGS Q34b) |
| ackOwnership | the source of truth sends the ACK after its own publication; read-your-own-write holds by routing (the pull at the returned position goes to an eligible index, else the fallback); in normal operation the current index is kept synchronous so the fast path serves that pull; during a current-index outage commits and ACKs continue, pulls fall back, the index catches up from the feed through a bounded queue, and fallback share and recovery time are measured (GS.04b); history and analytics stay asynchronous behind watermarks (RULINGS Q31e, replacing Q28's ACK clause) |
| layerSwaps | layers are swapped one at a time under matched workloads at small rungs (current-index candidates on P1 and P4; history candidates on past-basis reads and GS.12; source candidates on P2 and P3); only the two or three best compositions go on to end-to-end validation with the golden scenarios |
| scopeKey | an engine-scope receipt's key is (layer, the engine assigned to that layer, its image digest, configuration hash and slot), derived from the composition, never from engineOfLane |
| sourceDeclaration | every composition declares its source implementation: the source assignment carries variant engine-source or log-source (COMMIT_OUTCOMES), and a log source binds its log identity and durability configuration (implementationSha256, fsyncMode, fullFsync, device; LOG_FIELDS) next to the engine identities in every receipt (RULINGS Q55b) |
| readGuarantees | status: PROVISIONAL, flagged for Sam (RULINGS Q55c, superseding Q50b; the native half is replaced by Q58a); repository: repository pulls give read-your-own-write by routing (replica, else overlay, else the source's log), never below the caller's basis; with the replica unreachable they fall back to the source (RULINGS Q50a); native: PROVISIONAL, flagged for Sam (RULINGS Q58a, superseding Q55c's native half): native SPARQL, XTQL, SQL and Datalog go through a Triplex facade; engine ports are not a public surface. A request may carry after: position (wait until the replica marker reaches it within the deadline, then the typed E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE {required, observed, replica}) or at: position (exact; the engine must also reconstruct it, else the typed E-BASIS-NOT-RECONSTRUCTIBLE). A client session sends its own high-water mark (its last commit position and last read basis) as an implicit after. A tokenless external caller gets the replica's watermark and the reported position. Every answer carries {basis: {low, high}, route}. With the replica unreachable the answer is the typed E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE. The default deadline is 2 s; nativeDeadlineMs: 2000; honesty: no surface may present an answer as at a basis it was not computed at; testing: NS.P2 and G7.composition.ack-and-routed-ryow test each surface the composition claims against its own guarantee; NS.P2's repository read-your-own-write never establishes a native-surface guarantee |
| hotSubjects | a per-subject FIFO queue in the candidate's command router (bounded; the typed E-OVERLOADED beyond the bound, never an unbounded wait) with same-subject group commit (up to 8 queued commands of one subject in one engine transaction, positions by ordinal); optimistic compare-and-set stays for cross-node races; the queue is part of the candidate, never the driver (RULINGS Q51a) |
| brokerCurrentIndex | a broker-side current-entity index (the per-subject current document served from the host, QLever kept for history and analytics) is a candidate current-index layer for P4; EXP-Q05 builds and measures it (RULINGS Q50a) |
| brokerPromotion | before a log-source composition becomes a default it must close G7.broker.promotion-hardening: an overlay memory bound with backpressure (typed E-OVERLOADED beyond the bound) for replica outages of the GS.04b kind (RULINGS Q50d), and the SQLite substrate of RULINGS Q58c (replacing Q50d's segment rotation and file-lock items) with log erasure by crypto-shredding (RULINGS Q58e); an out-of-process broker and off-device copies are deferred; merging a broker behind a default-off option needs only the Q62a fixes, independently re-verified (RULINGS Q62b) |
| sharedVolumeFollower | rejected for promotion: XTDB 2.2.0's ReadOnlyLocalLog reads half-written records and dies permanently (9 deaths in 30 minutes), though it never answered wrongly; the second-writer guard and the follower harness stay; the torn-read repro joins the R21 upstream-filing question for Sam, and nothing is filed without him (RULINGS Q63a, Q63c) |
| parameterisedSql | seeders and appliers on XTDB use parameterised statements only; 1,000-row literal INSERTs exhausted a 2 GiB heap (EXP-X05), as per-cell expressions did in EXP-P2X (RULINGS Q63d) |
| currentPath | status: PROVISIONAL (RULINGS Q68); horizon: the default H trails head by one hour of positions (the 15% basis bucket); a pinned sweep or reconcile holds H at or below its pin; the broker refuses a new pin that would make H trail head by more than 24 hours (RULINGS Q68b); expired: facts whose valid_to has passed retire from the current structure through a valid-time horizon; EXP-P4 measures the 20% expired path (RULINGS Q68e); design: see experimentDirections EXP-P4 (RULINGS Q68a, Q68g) |
| incarnationFencing | single-request read surfaces read the replica marker in the same request as the answer; multi-request surfaces (Datalog, executor) use replica incarnation fencing: every replay begins by writing a new incarnation id, and an answer is accepted only if (incarnation, marker) is equal before and after (RULINGS Q67c) |
| overlay | the overlay merge is allowed for entity pulls only, keyed by id with the greater LSN winning, under a tested invariant (identity columns never change; a retraction is a new version); engine aggregates, Datalog and executor reads and paged lists never merge: they wait or fail typed; frames carry explicit tombstones, so erasure and deletes cannot resurrect replica rows (RULINGS Q58d) |
| experimentDirections | EXP-P2B: XTDB as a second replica behind the broker: one pgwire transaction per frame (ASSERT the marker, INSERT rows with a fixed _valid_from, INSERT the new marker; P0004 on guard failure); rows and marker read in one read-only transaction; the marker row is the eligibility authority; XTDB system time never carries broker positions; Local log first, InMemory log plus an epoch bump as an arm; predictions and measurements per R23 section 6; it starts after the Q62a fix round is re-verified, from the same author, so one writer owns the broker files (RULINGS Q58b; Q51b's original direction stays pending); broker-hardening: after EXP-P2B: the host log moves to SQLite through better-sqlite3 (WAL, synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=ON, checkpoint_fullfsync=ON, locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE, application-driven PASSIVE checkpoints, a worker thread when readers share the process), keeping a CRC32C prev-chain column, a committed_at column, an epoch row and the marker and checkpoint cross-checks (plain SQLite misses mid-WAL corruption); heads, claims and operations become tables; the overlay becomes a persisted recent_rows table; predictions H1 to H6 of R23 section 6.4 (RULINGS Q58c); P1-replicas: read scaling on both lanes comes from replicas fed by the broker (Q58b): each XTDB or QLever replica has its own applier and marker, so readers never touch the writer's log or indexer and the shared-log follower is unnecessary; EXP-P2B measures the first XTDB replica and a second-replica arm follows; Kafka (E8, about 7 GiB) is deferred (RULINGS Q63b); EXP-P4: provisional (RULINGS Q68a, Q68g): P4's fast path is one current structure holding live facts plus facts retired after a retention horizon H, served at basis B only when H <= B <= W (W its applied watermark), else the history path; its first copy lives in the broker, written with the frame (arm H1); engines get a smaller copy in the same transaction or guarded update (XTDB tx_current, QLever cur graph) for list and native queries; EXP-P4 measures arms A0, X1, X2, Q1 and H1 per R24 section 6, exactness gate first, and measures X1 (default temporal bounds) fresh and aged before any write-path change, because FOR ALL VALID_TIME on XTDB current reads forfeits the engine's current and historical split |

### 8.8 Erasure (TARGETS section 7, RULINGS Q24)

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| status | PROVISIONAL product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam: explain at a pre-erasure basis shows the marker, not the value |
| boundary | the boundary is the erasure commit's publication; a read that started before it sees, for each erasure commit, either all of that commit's values as they were or all as markers, never a mix (RULINGS Q52e, narrowing Q49d); every read that starts after it, at any basis including bases before the erasure, returns ErasedValue {erasedAt} in place of the value |
| shape | assertion identities and valid and record intervals keep their shape |
| reproduction | every reproduction contract holds modulo erasure: the C6 whole-journal comparison, raw and native query results, SDK results, cursor stability, bit-for-bit explain and GS.12; both sides of a comparison replace erased values with their markers before comparing (RULINGS Q31f) |
| frontier | an index or cache may serve any basis only after it has applied every erasure published so far, independently of the requested basis; an old-basis read never passes on the strength of its basis alone (RULINGS Q31f) |
| cacheInvalidation | erasure invalidates every old-basis cache entry that holds the erased value |
| keyEvidence | for crypto-shredding, the lane's inventory shows that every surviving copy of a protected value, and of anything derived from it, is encrypted only under the destroyed key; deleting some key is not evidence |
| derivedChannels | a PII attribute's order key and lexical channel are inside the encrypted envelope (range rules on PII then run in the kernel after decryption), or the attribute is not eligible for range rules |
| restore | the erasure ledger is kept apart from the data and replayed after any restore or rebuild |
| journalCommit | an erasure commit is an ordinary data-journal transaction: it has a position, a txId, a record in transactions() and its own :_tx/ facts, and its changes list only identities (entity, attribute, assertion ids), never values; it is also written to the erasure ledger kept apart from the data, which restore and rebuild replay; earlier transactions' :_tx/change facts for erased values show the ErasedValue marker, so ER-JOURNAL-MODULO compares markers on both sides (RULINGS Q49a) |
| idempotence | the first erasure of an identity sets erasedAt; erasing it again changes nothing; an erase that matches nothing still commits, as a journal record with an empty change list (RULINGS Q49b) |
| queries | provisional, under the Q24 flag for Sam: an erased value is present with no readable value; it matches no value predicate (equality, inequality, range, pattern), so a filter never selects or rejects a subject by it; SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip it while COUNT of assertions counts it; ORDER BY places erased markers last in a deterministic order by assertion id; grouping puts all erased values of an attribute in one group keyed by the marker; Unique ignores erased values; an erased reference cannot be followed (an include returns the marker) (RULINGS Q49c) |
| inFlight | an erasure commit is atomic for readers: a read that started before it published sees either all of that commit's values as they were or all as markers, never a mix (RULINGS Q52e, narrowing Q49d from per value to per commit); erasure commits become visible in position order, so a read that started before n in-flight erasure commits in its scope sees a prefix of them, and the acceptable answers are the n + 1 prefixes, never all 2^n subsets (RULINGS Q66a); a continuation cursor carries the erasure prefix its page was computed with, and every later page answers with that same prefix (RULINGS Q66b); only erasures in the read's own scope are in flight, erasures in other scopes always apply (RULINGS Q66c) |
| queriesResidual | provisional, under the Q24 flag for Sam: a count of distinct values counts an attribute's erased values as one value (the marker group), a count of assertions counts each erased assertion (Q52a); ORDER BY puts readable values first, then erased markers by assertion id, then missing values, in both directions (Q52b); a marker group reports the earliest erasedAt among its members (Q52c); an erased reference takes no part in reference constraints: it blocks no restrict delete, cascades nothing and is skipped by ReferenceTarget validation (Q52d) (RULINGS Q52) |
| commandShape | the op is spelled erase; erasure is a typed invalid-command error; an erase is its own command, and mixing it with other operations or giving it preconditions is a typed invalid-command error (RULINGS Q52g) |
| selectors | matches nothing (Q49b) means a well-formed entity or entity-plus-attribute selector with no assertions to erase, which commits with an empty change list; an erase naming an unknown assertion target or an unknown id is E-INVALID-VALUE, as for retract (Q56a); erase accepts the same selectors as retract, including {id: ...} (Q56f); retracting an already erased assertion by target commits and history shows the marker with the retraction's time, so erase then delete is supported (Q56g) (RULINGS Q56) |
| presence | an erased value is still a present assertion: a card-one attribute holding a readable and an erased value conflicts with E-CONFLICTING-VALUES as two readable values would, the remedy being to retract the erased assertion (Q56b); answers never depend on the erased value, so a readable SAME beside an erased support conflicts whatever the erased value was (Q56c); in a card-many value list erased markers come after the readable elements, ordered by assertion id (Q56d); Required is satisfied by an erased value (Q56e) (RULINGS Q56, provisional under the Q24 flag) |
| currentCopies | provisional: every current copy (the broker's current store, XTDB tx_current, the QLever cur graph) is covered by Q58e's per-subject keys; a QLever cur graph holds no personal-data literals (keys and references only, values from the encrypted host store) unless EXP-P4 shows a reindex-free erasure path (RULINGS Q68f) |
| logErasure | values held in the broker log, the recent_rows overlay and checkpoints are erasable: value payloads in frames are encrypted per subject and erasure destroys the key (crypto-shredding), so TARGETS 7 holds without rewriting the log; designed in the broker-hardening experiment (RULINGS Q58e) |
| syntheticData | in-flight outputs may hold pre-erasure values (Q49d, Q52e), so every oracle case, fixture and golden scenario uses synthetic values only; no real personal data enters the lab (RULINGS Q56h) |
| tests | ER-PINNED-READER, ER-REBUILD, ER-RESTORE-PRE-BACKUP, ER-ORACLE-POST |

Protected-copy inventory, per lane: source log and journal, current index, history index, analytical copy, order-key channels, lexical channels, QLever broker log of record, broker recent_rows overlay, current-value copies (broker current store, XTDB tx_current, QLever cur graph), caches, checkpoints, backups, observer outputs, old index generations, freed blocks.

### 8.9 Evaluator counterexamples (RULINGS Q26)

Every obligation declares at least one mode. 'single-execution' runs each selected case once, so executions equal selections; NS and GS obligations use it explicitly (RULINGS Q26). 'paired-rounds' (NS obligations, RULINGS Q60f) runs every comparison under PAIR_0: paired rounds of A0 and candidate, never a single run. Other modes (current, reopen, engine-restart) each run every selected case once more. A secondary threshold (RULINGS Q25) is measured and reported against its value every run; missing it never fails or blocks an obligation, and it never feeds a closure rule other than CR-METRICS.

| Id | Defeats | Receipt set | Why it stays OPEN |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CX-CALIBRATION-EMPTY | CR-CALIBRATION | a VC record with an empty values list | an empty requirement set fails closed |
| CX-CALIBRATION-MISSING | CR-CALIBRATION, CR-NS | a VC record that omits one threshold an NS obligation names | every named threshold needs a record |
| CX-NS-MISSING-BAR | CR-NS | an ns-run with no measurement for one named bar | a missing bar is not a met bar |

### 8.10 Position coordinates and gates (TARGETS 4.1, RULINGS Q31c, Q31i)

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| coordinates | (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal): the source of truth's log stream and epoch, the engine's log offset (or the QLever broker's log frame) and the ordinal of a Triplex transact inside that engine transaction |
| order | lexicographic over (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal); positions need not be dense |
| nested | one engine transaction holding several Triplex transacts gives them consecutive ordinals at one offset, assigned atomically with the assertions and the subject compare-and-set |
| watermark | a fully resolved prefix: every position at or below it is applied or known aborted (stronger than the greatest position seen) |
| aborted | aborted offsets are accounted: the feed's resolution stream lists each one |
| epochs | a watermark from one epoch never satisfies a basis in another epoch without the mapping C1 defines |
| oracle | O-REPLAY treats positions as totally ordered coordinates: it sorts by coordinate and assigns its own dense ordinals for cuts |
| falsifiers | FX-NESTED-CUTS, FX-ABORT-GAP, FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION, FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP |
| binding | the core binds a transaction's position after the source of truth publishes it; a position is an opaque, totally ordered value (bigint) that preserves the (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal) order, so adapters never return placeholders and no ordinal packing limit exists; lands with the broker's engine-agnostic extraction (EXP-P2B) on both lanes (RULINGS Q51c) |
| falsifierText | {"FX-NESTED-CUTS": "cuts at every interior ordinal of one engine transaction holding several Triplex transacts", "FX-ABORT-GAP": "an aborted offset between two committed ones: cuts on both sides and the resolution-stream entry", "FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION": "a crash between appending a transaction and resolving it (applied or aborted)", "FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP": "a feed consumer resuming from a checkpoint that sits at an abort gap"} |

| Gate | Rule | Requires | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GATE-POSITION | no comparative or promotion claim on any composition, A0 included, until a VA-valid G7.position.coordinates receipt for that composition's source covers POSITION_REQUIRED_CASES, the four falsifiers included; no source-hash allowlist or declared density grants an exemption (RULINGS Q31c, Q38a; OUTSIDE_BLOCK_MUTATION_FIXTURE shows why) | G7.position.coordinates | NS.* and GS.* obligations and every comparative or promotion claim (CLAIM_ADMISSION) |
| GATE-W0 | no domain-dependent obligation closes until V-D01 has independently reviewed W0 (SPEC.md, releases, golden cases), every W0_PIN hash is pinned in this contract (RULINGS Q31i, Q48a) and O-DOMAIN has reproduced the population fingerprint (RULINGS Q40g); a null field fails closed | W0_PIN complete, W0.coverage-floors | every obligation whose oracles include O-DOMAIN |
| GATE-ORACLE-PIN | an obligation whose expected answers come from an oracle closes only once ORACLE_PINS pins that oracle's files with an acceptance receipt, the obligation is not in the pin's excludes, and the oracle does not refuse any case it selects (oracle_scope); a null pin fails closed (V-O02 C1, RULINGS Q45a, Q45b) | ORACLE_PINS complete for every oracle the obligation uses | every obligation using an oracle listed in ORACLE_PINS (O-REPLAY, O-TDK1) |
| GATE-BROKER-HARDENING | no promotion claim that makes a log-source composition a default until G7.broker.promotion-hardening is closed for it (RULINGS Q50d, Q58c, Q62b); merging it behind a default-off option needs only the Q62a fixes, independently re-verified | G7.broker.promotion-hardening | promotion claims on log-source compositions (CLAIM_ADMISSION) |
| GATE-TDK1-VECTORS | G1.decimal.tdk1-differential closes only once TDK1_VECTOR_PIN names a reviewed vector file by sha256; a null pin fails closed (RULINGS Q35, R20 V5) | TDK1_VECTOR_PIN complete | G1.decimal.tdk1-differential |

No density exemption (RULINGS Q38a): every composition, A0 included, needs PO-LEXICOGRAPHIC-ORDER, PO-ORACLE-DENSE-ORDINALS, PO-NESTED-CUTS-DENSE, FX-NESTED-CUTS, FX-ABORT-GAP, FX-CRASH-APPEND-RESOLUTION, FX-RESUME-AT-ABORT-GAP, PO-ABORTED-LISTED. Evidence that a source-hash allowlist was unsafe: the exported withTransaction binding (about line 485) is rebound in memory to allocate an extra position before executing the transaction; all five 0.3.4 block hashes stayed unchanged and the old check returned dense, falsifiers skipped (0.3.4 density_proven returned True); now the four falsifiers run; FX-NESTED-CUTS fails under the mutation (mutant M-WITHTRANSACTION-REBIND).


when any comparative or promotion claim is admitted, including one from a screening (P-SCREEN) run, the verdict comes only from the evaluator's own QUALIFICATION_RUN at the claimed commit (RULINGS Q55a); records an experiment or the claimant supplies, never from supplied case names or Booleans, are diagnostics only. The evaluator builds the declared tree and requires: a passing G7.position.coordinates run for that build and composition over POSITION_REQUIRED_CASES; G10.composition.identity-bound with every assignment bound (engine, image digest, configuration hash, slot) and the source's protocol variant declared, a log source binding its log identity and durability configuration (RULINGS Q55b); where any claimed obligation uses O-DOMAIN, the W0 pin accepted through VERIFIER_REGISTRY, the O-DOMAIN fingerprint pinned by a reviewed contract version (never from the claim, RULINGS Q55e) and a passing W0.coverage-floors run; every oracle the claim or its prerequisites use pinned and accepted through VERIFIER_REGISTRY, with the claimed obligation outside that pin's excludes and refusals. Cases are resolved from the pinned manifests, every case in every mode; expected answers come from running the pinned oracle, so an oracle exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED never counts as PASS; the declared comparator decides. The control is A0 from the A0_REGISTRY entry for the claim's source engine, rebuilt by the evaluator to the registry's binarySha256 and run on the same evaluator-chosen workload (WORKLOAD_IDENTITY) as paired rounds, each arm on its own registered slot and placement (RULINGS Q46b, Q47b, Q60, Q67g); a promotion claim is rejected explicitly until its prerequisites are enforced (RULINGS Q67j); while that entry is null every comparison is a diagnostic. Independent verification of the claimed obligation counts only through a VERIFIER_REGISTRY entry for that obligation and commit. Unknown obligation ids are rejected, never dropped. lab/bin/claim.mjs implements this (EXP-E01) with these functions as the reference model. A claim with a failed or pending prerequisite is a diagnostic, never a qualified winner; while O-REPLAY's pin is null every claim is a diagnostic, and A0 measurements may run and produce diagnostics, never closures (RULINGS Q34d, Q37b, Q38b).


| Evidence record (RULINGS Q47a) | Fields | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| build-manifest/1 | schema, sourceTreeSha256, binarySha256, modules | binds the source tree to the executed binary; the binary and every executed or imported module ({path, sha256}, at least one) are retained objects whose bytes hash to the listed values |
| verifier-record/1 | schema, obligation, definitionSha256, verifier, verdict | names the receipt's obligation and definition hash, a nonempty verifier and the verdict ACCEPT |
| build-manifest/2 | schema, sourceTreeSha256, binarySha256, modules, inputs, buildSpecSha256 | build-manifest/1 plus the build inputs ({path, sha256}, every one checked against the side's commit) and the hash of the contract's BUILD_SPEC (RULINGS Q61f) |
| case-result/2 | schema, obligation, case, selection, oracle, oracleExit, oracleCode, expectedSha256, observedSha256, mode, rep, comparator, inputSha256 | case-result/1 plus the mode, the repetition, the comparator applied and the input's sha256; a run that cannot be expressed in this record fails closed (RULINGS Q61e); a case reached by several select entries records the first select entry in contract order (RULINGS Q65c); its verdict is recomputed with its declared comparator on the retained raw objects, never by hash equality (RULINGS Q67i, Q71c) |
| oracle-invocation/1 | schema, oracle, pinCommit, argvSha256, runtime, inputSha256, exit, outputSha256 | one record per oracle invocation, with the runtime that ran it (for a Python oracle, its version), because an answer can depend on it (RULINGS Q71b) |
| fault-witness/1 | schema, obligation, case, mode, rep, faultPointId, injectedAt, lastWitnessedTransition, eventsSha256 | one retained record per fault injection (the injector's point and time, the last transition with durable evidence, and the retained transition events), never a faultReps count alone (RULINGS Q61j; EVIDENCE_KINDS fault-witness) |
| case-result/1 | schema, obligation, case, selection, oracle, oracleExit, oracleCode, expectedSha256, observedSha256 | the retained raw oracle run and observation for one case and the selection it covers; PASS only when oracleExit is 0, oracleCode is null, the expected and observed objects are both retained and equal; an oracle exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED is a refusal and never PASS (RULINGS Q45b, Q47a) |

Workload identity (RULINGS Q47b): every measurement and control receipt carries workload {generatorSourceSha256 (trace generator hash), seed, offerScheduleSha256, window [from, to] with 0 <= from < to, slot (the source assignment's slot)}, every field present, typed and nonempty; a control matches a measurement only when the two workload identities are equal field by field; a missing field never matches a missing field (RULINGS Q47b).


**Qualification run (RULINGS Q55a).** a QUALIFIED verdict comes only from a run the evaluator executes itself at the claimed commit; every record an experiment or a claimant supplies (receipts, case results, manifests, selections, verifier records, fingerprints) is DIAGNOSTIC evidence only (RULINGS Q55a).

| Step | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| build | build the declared source tree at the claimed commit, and A0 from the A0_REGISTRY entry's tree and commit; record the evaluator's own build hashes; the A0 build must reproduce the registry's binarySha256 |
| resolve | resolve cases from the pinned case-set manifests (CS manifestSha256): every case of each selected set, tag or named case, in every declared mode; a claimant's selection or case list is ignored; an unpinned or mismatching manifest, or a selection that resolves to no case, leaves the obligation unresolved (DIAGNOSTIC) |
| execute | run the system under test through the gate on a registered slot whose images are the contract's IMAGE_PINS; in a CR-FAULT obligation every faultPoint case is injected T-FAULT-REPS times per mode, each injection retained as a fault-witness/1 record (RULINGS Q61i, Q61j) |
| expect | compute every expected answer by running the pinned, accepted oracle on the pinned case input; a refusal (exit 2 or X-NOT-MODELED) fails the obligation closed |
| compare | apply the comparator the case declares (COMPARATORS) to the expected answer and the observation |
| control | for CR-NS and CR-GS obligations only, run the frozen trace (load-contract writerTrace.generator.frozen) as paired rounds under PAIR_0 against the candidate build and the A0 build on identically configured registered slots (RULINGS Q60, Q61g, Q61h); the A0 side is verified through the A0_REGISTRY entry's measuredBy (RULINGS Q61k) |
| verify | count independent verification only through VERIFIER_REGISTRY entries for the subject and commit |
| record | retain builds, inputs, oracle outputs, observations, fault witnesses and verdicts as content-addressed records written by the evaluator: build-manifest/2, case-result/2 and fault-witness/1 (RULINGS Q61e, Q61f, Q61j; the /1 formats of RULINGS Q54e stay readable) |

**Evaluator inputs (RULINGS Q61).** Contract source: the evaluator reads obligations.json and load-contract.json from its own clone at an explicitly supplied immutable authority commit, never --authority-ref main (Q86e supersedes Q61a lookup); never from the claimed commit; VERIFIER_REGISTRY is read as written (Q61b). Executing isolation integration remains deferred to G03.. Oracle runners: O-REPLAY argv python3 -I lab/oracles/replay/cli.py {case}; O-DOMAIN argv python3 -I lab/oracles/domain/cli.py run {case}; O-CONTRACT argv python3 -I -B lab/acceptance/build_contract.py --oracle O-CONTRACT {case}; O-OBS argv python3 -I -B lab/acceptance/oracle/observe.py check {protocol} {case} --contract {contract} --context {context} --bundle {bundle} --key-file {key}. Answer extraction: Q75g: row comparators apply to each queries[i].result or queries[i].inFlight.acceptable[j].result: bare arrays, rows arrays inside {cut, rows}, or both raw and snapshot arrays inside match/entityTriples results; all wrapper metadata (including cut, count and contract) compares exactly. Unknown row-bearing object shapes are uncomparable and fail closed. UTF-8 strings compare by code point without normalization. commandOutcomes and state compare exactly. The evaluator runs the runner's argv with {case} replaced by the path of the pinned case input (and {mode} by the mode where the argv names it) in a directory holding only the pinned oracle files; exit 2, or X-NOT-MODELED on stdout or stderr, is a refusal; any other nonzero exit is an oracle error; neither is ever PASS; on exit 0 stdout is one canonical JSON document (UTF-8, key-sorted, the exact bytes of its own canonical form after one trailing newline is removed), and for O-REPLAY the expected answer is the object of the report's commandOutcomes, state and queries members, the report's own identity and verdict fields (format, oracle, caseId, caseSha256, lane, verdict, divergedAtCommand, receiptConsistency, rulesInEffect, reservedNamespaces) not being part of it; a case input given to the oracle carries no expectations of its own (RULINGS Q61c).

| id | nonempty string, unique in the manifest |
| tags | list of strings |
| input | repository-relative path of the case input file |
| contentSha256 | sha256 of the input file's bytes |
| comparator | a COMPARATORS id |
| oracle (optional) | optional: an oracle id among the obligation's oracles (default: the obligation's first oracle) |
| faultPoint (optional) | optional Boolean: the case is a fault point, injected T-FAULT-REPS times with a retained fault-witness/1 per injection |

**Measurement protocol PAIR-0 (RULINGS Q60, provisional).** comparisons run as paired rounds: a duet (A0 and candidate at the same time on two identically configured slots, same trace window) or, as the fallback, same-engine ABBA; a single run never decides a bar (RULINGS Q60a); margins: the lower bound of A/B at or above the claimed ratio (1.25 by default); the upper bound of B/A at or below 1.10 for p50 and 1.15 for p99. measurement slots run with a cpuset and no CPU quota; receipts record the effective cpu.max, cpuset and cpu.weight; quota and cpuset arms are never compared; A0 is measured again under the new regime (RULINGS Q60c) latency histograms include every offered command (expired, failed and rejected ones at their censor time) next to the committed-only view; reads get an open-loop probe at a fixed rate; per-second goodput and per-second maximum latency are recorded (RULINGS Q60d) absolute bars are judged only in GREEN windows (the pre-registered noise signals and the A/A gate of R22 section 4.2); outside them an absolute bar is reported unjudged, which never counts as met (RULINGS Q60e) a screening trace with a burst every 180 s is a new comparison series (TARGETS 2.1 item 5), so P2 and P3 rounds contain enough commands for p99; acceptance keeps the frozen trace (RULINGS Q60g) a measurement window takes every heavy token and freezes pool admission for its duration (RULINGS Q60h) EXP-N01's single-run A0 is diagnostic only; A0 numbers for comparisons come from paired rounds (RULINGS Q60i)

## 10. Obligations by section

### Goal 1. Exact value kinds, schemas, cardinality, uniqueness, references

**`G1.found.unchanged44`: Unchanged44 on the lane foundation.**
- Statement: The unchanged 44-case shared conformance suite (CS-U44) passes against the lane engine's Triples foundation in current and reopened form: 44 named cases per mode, zero skipped.
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-U44 (all, EXISTS).
- Oracles: O-TESTKIT (EXISTS). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen; params {"gates": []}.
- Sources: wiki/goals.md:20-23; lab/research/R4-codebase-harness-map.md 5.3.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G1.types.value-kinds-roundtrip`: Every value kind in use round-trips exactly on every surface.**
- Statement: Every case of CS-TYPES8 (one assertion per value kind of VALUE_KINDS with the listed edge values, integers inside the lane's declared range) reads back exactly through Triples, the repository, the lane's native surface with a schema-derived contract, and the documented raw recipe, in current, reopen and engine-restart modes.
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-TYPES8 (all, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-RAW-HATCH. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-INTEGER-ROUND, M-NEGZERO.
- Sources: lab/SCOPE.md section 2 item 4; lab/research/SAM-pasted-numbers-2026-11-07.md section 5; lab/research/R2-qlever-capabilities.md 4.1.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G1.types.out-of-range-rejected`: Values a lane cannot hold fail with a typed error, never silently.**
- Statement: Every lane accepts every integer in [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1]; on every qualified write route (the Triplex writer, the bulk import lane, replay and restore: RANGE-OUT-WRITER, RANGE-OUT-BULK, RANGE-OUT-REPLAY, RANGE-OUT-RESTORE) every CS-RANGE-OUT case (integers beyond the lane's declared LANE_INTEGER_RANGE, for QLever beyond +/-2^59) fails atomically with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE before any mutation, with no residue on any access path, and is never wrapped, widened or rounded. Bare native wire access is a diagnostic surface, not a qualified route: QLever's native wrap there is matrix row 51 (KNOWN-LIMIT KL-Q1) and diagnostic D-Q-INT60, never a failure of this obligation (RULINGS Q23).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-RANGE-OUT (all, TO-AUTHOR); CS-RANGE-OUT (RANGE-OUT-WRITER, RANGE-OUT-BULK, RANGE-OUT-REPLAY, RANGE-OUT-RESTORE, TO-AUTHOR); CS-RANGE-OUT (RANGE-OUT-RETRACT-PATTERN, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-TRIPLES, EP-WRITER, EP-BULK, EP-REPLAY. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen; params {"diagnostics": ["D-Q-INT60"], "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-OUT-OF-RANGE-WRAP.
- Sources: lab/research/SAM-pasted-numbers-2026-11-07.md section 5; lab/TARGETS.md section 3; lab/acceptance/RULINGS.md superseded section.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G1.types.decimal`: Decimal value kind for money and business decimals.**
- Statement: Every CS-DECIMAL case, per DECIMAL_RULES (RULINGS Q18) and the operation, conversion and scale tables DECIMAL_OPS, DECIMAL_CONVERSIONS and DECIMAL_SCALE_EVOLUTION (RULINGS Q22), one named case per row, plus DECIMAL_TESTS (adjacent large decimals, negatives, zero, scale boundaries, arithmetic intermediates, every query and serialization path, an independent order-key check, and input capture before normalization): each decimal attribute declares precision and scale; every precision is stored as the TDK1 key plus derived canonical text (RULINGS Q35b; the key bytes themselves are checked by G1.decimal.tdk1-admission and G1.decimal.tdk1-serialization under O-TDK1, RULINGS Q45c), compared exactly across attributes of different declared scale (DEC-CROSS-SCALE-COMPARE), and round-trips exactly on every surface; a decimal on an undeclared attribute (DEC-UNDECLARED-ATTRIBUTE) and -0.00 (DEC-NEGZERO-REFUSED) fail with E-INVALID-VALUE; 16.500 fits scale 2 and reads back as 16.50 (DEC-TRAILING-ZERO-FITS); toDecimal starts from the exact binary expansion (DEC-TODECIMAL-EXACT-EXPANSION); AVG over decimal fails with E-DECIMAL-AVG unless written with divide (DEC-AVG-PREFLIGHT) (RULINGS Q33b); every comparison with integer or number, equality included, is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY (DEC-CROSS-FAMILY-PREFLIGHT) and exact after explicit conversion (DEC-CONVERTED-COMPARE); results beyond the precision fail with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW, bare / with E-DECIMAL-BARE-DIVIDE, decimal to integer with a fraction with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION, and a narrowing migration that would lose digits with E-DECIMAL-NARROWING, atomically; range rules (for example 'pay rate at or above 16.50') compare in exact numeric order on the repository, fragments and documented raw channel; a value with more fractional digits than the scale fails with E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (DEC-SCALE-EXCESS) and one outside the precision with E-DECIMAL-OVERFLOW (DEC-PRECISION-EXCESS), never rounded; kernel arithmetic over decimals is exact.
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.

### Goal 7. Atomic writes, receipts, migration and evolution, recovery

**`G7.outbox.publication-sequence`: Outbox deliveries are keyed by (id, publication sequence).**
- Statement: Per OUTBOX (RULINGS Q38f): the delivery key is (id, publication sequence); the sequence increments whenever the payload to publish differs from the latest published payload for that id, so a release rollback R1, R2, R1 publishes three deliveries 1650, 1700, 1650 (OB-RELEASE-ROLLBACK); publication state is persisted atomically with its outbox record (OB-ATOMIC-STATE); a crash before delivery replays the same identity exactly once (OB-CRASH-BEFORE-DELIVERY); an unchanged activation during recovery publishes nothing new while the pending delivery keeps its identity (OB-UNCHANGED-ACTIVATION-RECOVERY); a correction revert publishes a new sequence (OB-CORRECTION-REVERT); an older-basis evaluation publishes nothing (OB-OLDER-BASIS-NO-DELIVERY, RULINGS Q40d); a retired id that reappears publishes a new sequence even with an unchanged payload (OB-RETIREMENT-REAPPEAR, RULINGS Q40h); only live reconciles at the current basis are published (OB-PREVIEW-NOT-PUBLISHED, RULINGS Q44c).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-OUTBOX (all, TO-AUTHOR); CS-OUTBOX (OB-CORRECTION-REVERT, OB-OLDER-BASIS-NO-DELIVERY, OB-RETIREMENT-REAPPEAR, OB-PREVIEW-NOT-PUBLISHED, OB-RELEASE-ROLLBACK, OB-CRASH-BEFORE-DELIVERY, OB-UNCHANGED-ACTIVATION-RECOVERY, OB-ATOMIC-STATE, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-DOMAIN (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-OUTBOX, EP-WRITER, EP-KERNEL. Profiles: P-FAULT.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-FAULT + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; thresholds T-FAULT-REPS; params {"gates": ["GATE-W0", "GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-OUTBOX-VERSION-DEDUP, M-OUTBOX-RETIREMENT-IGNORED.
- Sources: RULINGS Q38f; RULINGS Q40c; RULINGS Q40d; RULINGS Q40h; RULINGS Q44c; lab/reviews/plan-v2-round4.codex.md finding 8.
- Status: OPEN.

**`G7.outbox.receiver-ordering`: Receivers apply deliveries by publication sequence.**
- Statement: Per OUTBOX receivers (RULINGS Q42b, Q44d): a state projection records the highest sequence applied and never regresses (RX-REVERSED-ARRIVAL); an effect needing every transition recovers gaps from the outbox first (RX-GAP-RECOVERY); deduplication is persisted atomically with the receiver's state or effect (RX-RESTART-MID-SEQUENCE, RX-DEDUP-1-1-3-3-2); a receiver started after pruning is seeded from a snapshot (RX-LATE-START); O-DOMAIN's receive operation gives the expected receiver state.

**`G7.commit.protocol-transitions`: Commit outcomes follow the witnessed transition table.**

**`G7.broker.promotion-hardening`: A log-source composition is hardened before promotion.**
- Statement: Per COMPOSITION brokerPromotion (RULINGS Q50d), for a log-source composition: the overlay has a memory bound with backpressure, so a replica outage of the GS.04b kind returns the typed E-OVERLOADED beyond the bound and never grows without limit (BR-OVERLAY-BOUND-OVERLOADED); per RULINGS Q58c, replacing Q50d's rotation and lock items, the log is SQLite through better-sqlite3 with WAL, synchronous=FULL, fullfsync=ON, checkpoint_fullfsync=ON, locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE and application-driven PASSIVE checkpoints, a second writer being refused (BR-SQLITE-DURABILITY-PRAGMAS); a CRC32C prev-chain column detects mid-WAL corruption plain SQLite misses (BR-CRC-CHAIN-MID-WAL); every frame records committed_at (BR-COMMITTED-AT); an epoch row closes the previous epoch (BR-EPOCH-ROW); the marker and checkpoint are cross-checked against the log on open (BR-MARKER-CHECKPOINT-CROSSCHECK); the overlay is the persisted recent_rows table (BR-RECENT-ROWS-PERSISTED); and per RULINGS Q58e value payloads in frames, recent_rows and checkpoints are encrypted per subject, so erasure destroys the key (BR-LOG-CRYPTO-SHRED).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-BROKER (hardening, TO-AUTHOR); CS-BROKER (BR-OVERLAY-BOUND-OVERLOADED, BR-SQLITE-DURABILITY-PRAGMAS, BR-CRC-CHAIN-MID-WAL, BR-COMMITTED-AT, BR-EPOCH-ROW, BR-MARKER-CHECKPOINT-CROSSCHECK, BR-RECENT-ROWS-PERSISTED, BR-LOG-CRYPTO-SHRED, TO-AUTHOR); CS-BROKER (CONTRACT-Q84A, TO-AUTHOR); CS-BROKER (CONTRACT-Q84B, TO-AUTHOR); CS-BROKER (CONTRACT-Q84C, TO-AUTHOR); CS-BROKER (CONTRACT-Q84D, TO-AUTHOR); CS-BROKER (CONTRACT-Q84E, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-OBS (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-ENGINE-ADMIN, EP-ENGINE-OBS. Profiles: P-FAULT.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-OBSERVE; modes single-execution; params {"gates": []}.

**`G7.composition.ack-and-routed-ryow`: ACK after source publication; read-your-own-write by routing.**
- Statement: Per COMPOSITION ackOwnership (RULINGS Q31e, replacing Q28's ACK clause): the source of truth sends every ACK after its own publication (CO-ACK-AFTER-SOURCE-PUBLICATION, OBS-ACK-ORDER); the pull at the returned position is served by an index eligible for it, else by the fallback, so read-your-own-write is exact (CO-RYOW-ROUTED); during a current-index outage commits and ACKs continue and pulls fall back (CO-OUTAGE-ACKS-CONTINUE), and the index catches up from the feed through a bounded queue (CO-CATCHUP-BOUNDED-QUEUE). Per COMPOSITION fallbackEquivalence (RULINGS Q34b) and readGuarantees (RULINGS Q55c, provisional, flagged for Sam; supersedes Q50b), each serving surface the composition claims in the lane's language is tested against its own guarantee (CO-RYOW-PER-SURFACE): repository pulls read their own write by routing and fall back to the source with the replica down (CO-REPO-REPLICA-DOWN-FALLBACK); native answers report their basis (CO-NATIVE-REPORTS-BASIS), are never below a basis token (CO-NATIVE-BASIS-TOKEN-WAIT) or fail with E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE after the request deadline (CO-NATIVE-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE), answer at the replica's watermark without a token (CO-NATIVE-NO-TOKEN-WATERMARK) and fail with E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE with the replica down (CO-NATIVE-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE); no surface presents an answer as at a basis it was not computed at (CO-NO-FALSE-BASIS). Per COMPOSITION readGuarantees native (RULINGS Q58a, provisional, flagged for Sam; supersedes Q55c's native half): native queries go only through the Triplex facade (CO-FACADE-ONLY); an after: token waits for the replica marker within the deadline, then fails with E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE {required, observed, replica} (CO-NATIVE-AFTER-TOKEN); an at: token is exact (CO-NATIVE-AT-EXACT) or fails with E-BASIS-NOT-RECONSTRUCTIBLE (CO-NATIVE-AT-NOT-RECONSTRUCTIBLE); a session sends its high-water mark as an implicit after (CO-SESSION-HIGH-WATER); every answer carries {basis: {low, high}, route} (CO-ANSWER-BASIS-RANGE-ROUTE); the default deadline is 2 s (CO-NATIVE-DEFAULT-DEADLINE). Per V-P2Q (RULINGS Q62a): Datalog and executor reads inside a transaction wait for the replica to reach the transaction's source position or fail typed (CO-EXECUTOR-IN-TX-WAITS-OR-TYPED), and executor reads are scope-wide in the compare-and-set read set (CO-EXECUTOR-READS-IN-CAS-SET); after a replica regression the real marker is read with the answer and nothing is answered below the basis (CO-REPLICA-REGRESSION-REAL-MARKER); a pull beyond the resolved prefix waits or fails with E-BASIS-NOT-AVAILABLE, on A0 too (CO-PULL-BEYOND-PREFIX-TYPED); during an outage pulls and retraction-target reads fall back to the log or fail with E-REPLICA-UNAVAILABLE (CO-OUTAGE-PULL-FALLBACK, CO-OUTAGE-RETRACTION-TARGET-FALLBACK). Per RULINGS Q67c: single-request surfaces read the replica marker in the same request as the answer, and multi-request surfaces (Datalog, executor) use replica incarnation fencing, accepting an answer only if (incarnation, marker) is equal before and after, the reset-during-query interleaving being an independently authored case (CO-RESET-DURING-QUERY); per RULINGS Q67h every such error has one representation, _tag BasisNotAvailable or ReplicaUnavailable with {required, observed, replica} and an optional cause (CO-TYPED-ERROR-SHAPE); both cases' manifests stay null until the design is built; a stale fallback is rejected (CO-STALE-FALLBACK-REJECTED); a cross-language fallback recipe is bound to the same semantic query identity (parameters, basis, meaning) and the same oracle answer (CO-CROSS-LANGUAGE-RECIPE-IDENTITY), with total request latency and language attribution recorded.
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.

**`G7.position.coordinates`: Positions are totally ordered coordinates with a fully resolved watermark.**
- Statement: Per POSITION: a position is (stream, epoch, offset, ordinal), ordered lexicographically and not necessarily dense (PO-LEXICOGRAPHIC-ORDER); several Triplex transacts in one engine transaction take consecutive ordinals at one offset, assigned atomically with their assertions and the subject compare-and-set (PO-NESTED-CUTS-DENSE); a watermark is a fully resolved prefix and every aborted offset is listed in the feed's resolution stream (PO-ABORTED-LISTED); O-REPLAY sorts by coordinate and assigns its own dense ordinals for cuts (PO-ORACLE-DENSE-ORDINALS). **`G9.erasure.visibility-boundary`: Erasure is a visibility boundary at the erasure commit's publication.**
- Statement: Every CS-ERASURE boundary, marker and reproduction case per ERASURE: a read that started before the erasure published sees each erasure commit whole, all old values or all markers (ER-INFLIGHT-READ covers a commit erasing one value, identical under Q49d and Q52e; a commit erasing several is G9.erasure.residual-shapes' ER-INFLIGHT-ALL-OR-NONE, RULINGS Q52e); every read that starts after it, at any basis including bases before the erasure, returns ErasedValue {erasedAt} in place of the value (ER-AFTER-PUBLICATION-ALL-BASES), with assertion identities and valid and record intervals unchanged (ER-SHAPE-KEPT); a reader already pinned when the erasure lands follows the same rule (ER-PINNED-READER); an index or cache serves any basis only after applying every published erasure, independently of the basis (ER-FRONTIER-OLD-BASIS), and erasure invalidates every old-basis cache entry holding the value (ER-CACHE-INVALIDATION); expected post-erasure answers come independently from O-REPLAY (ER-ORACLE-POST).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (boundary, marker, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-INFLIGHT-READ, ER-AFTER-PUBLICATION-ALL-BASES, ER-SHAPE-KEPT, ER-PINNED-READER, ER-ORACLE-POST, ER-FRONTIER-OLD-BASIS, ER-CACHE-INVALIDATION, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-TRIPLES. Profiles: P-TINY-CONC.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL + CR-MUTANT-KILL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Mutation controls: M-ERASURE-FRONTIER-SKIP.

**`G9.erasure.protected-copies`: Erasure reaches every protected copy.**
- Statement: Each lane keeps a protected-copy inventory covering every PROTECTED_COPY_INVENTORY location, a log-source composition's log frames, recent_rows overlay and checkpoints included, which erase by crypto-shredding (ER-LOG-CRYPTO-SHRED, RULINGS Q58e); after the erasure publishes, OBS-ERASURE-SCAN finds no plaintext and no derived-channel copy in any of them, or, for crypto-shredding, evidence that every surviving copy of the value and of anything derived from it is encrypted only under the destroyed per-subject key (ER-KEY-EXCLUSIVE; deleting some key is not evidence); a PII attribute's order key and lexical channel are inside the encrypted envelope or the attribute is not eligible for range rules (ER-ORDER-KEY-CHANNEL, ER-LEXICAL-CHANNEL).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (inventory, derived-channels, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-ORDER-KEY-CHANNEL, ER-LEXICAL-CHANNEL, ER-KEY-EXCLUSIVE, ER-LOG-CRYPTO-SHRED, TO-AUTHOR).

**`G9.erasure.restore-reapplies`: Restore and rebuild re-apply the erasure ledger.**

**`G9.erasure.commit-semantics`: An erasure commit is an ordinary, idempotent journal transaction.**
- Statement: Per ERASURE journalCommit and idempotence (RULINGS Q49a, Q49b): an erasure commit has a position, a txId, a record in transactions() and its own :_tx/ facts, and its changes list only identities (entity, attribute, assertion ids), never values (ER-COMMIT-JOURNAL-IDENTITY-ONLY); it is also written to the erasure ledger kept apart from the data, which restore and rebuild replay (ER-COMMIT-LEDGER); earlier transactions' :_tx/change facts for erased values show the ErasedValue marker (ER-EARLIER-CHANGE-MARKER); the first erasure of an identity sets erasedAt and erasing it again changes nothing (ER-IDEMPOTENT-REERASE); an erase that matches nothing (a well-formed selector with no assertions to erase) still commits a journal record with an empty change list (ER-EMPTY-ERASURE-RECORD); an erase naming an unknown target or id is E-INVALID-VALUE (ER-ERASE-UNKNOWN-TARGET, RULINGS Q56a); erase accepts retract's selectors, {id: ...} included (ER-ERASE-BY-ID, Q56f); retracting an already erased assertion commits and history shows the marker with the retraction's time (ER-RETRACT-AFTER-ERASE, Q56g); all values are synthetic (ERASURE syntheticData, Q56h).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope engine. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (commit, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-COMMIT-JOURNAL-IDENTITY-ONLY, ER-COMMIT-LEDGER, ER-EARLIER-CHANGE-MARKER, ER-IDEMPOTENT-REERASE, ER-EMPTY-ERASURE-RECORD, ER-ERASE-UNKNOWN-TARGET, ER-ERASE-BY-ID, ER-RETRACT-AFTER-ERASE, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-TRIPLES, EP-REPLAY. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen, engine-restart; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
- Sources: lab/TARGETS.md section 7 items 1 and 5; RULINGS Q24; RULINGS Q49a, Q49b.
- Notes: Provisional product ruling (RULINGS Q24), flagged for Sam; the loop proceeds on it.

**`G9.erasure.query-semantics`: Erased values give deterministic query answers.**
- Statement: Per ERASURE queries (RULINGS Q49c, provisional under the Q24 flag for Sam), on the repository, the native surface in the lane language and the raw recipes: an erased value is present with no readable value; it matches no value predicate (equality, inequality, range, pattern), so a filter never selects or rejects a subject by it (ER-PREDICATE-NO-MATCH); SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX skip it while COUNT of assertions counts it (ER-AGGREGATE-SKIP-COUNT); ORDER BY places erased markers last, in a deterministic order by assertion id (ER-ORDER-MARKERS-LAST); grouping puts all erased values of an attribute in one group keyed by the marker (ER-GROUP-ONE-MARKER); Unique ignores erased values (ER-UNIQUE-IGNORES); an erased reference cannot be followed and an include returns the marker (ER-REFERENCE-MARKER). Per ERASURE presence (RULINGS Q56b to Q56e): a card-one attribute with a readable and an erased value conflicts with E-CONFLICTING-VALUES (ER-CARD-ONE-READABLE-AND-ERASED), also when the readable value equals what the erased support held (ER-EQUAL-SUPPORT-ERASED-CONFLICTS); card-many markers follow the readable elements by assertion id (ER-CARD-MANY-MARKERS-LAST); Required is satisfied by an erased value (ER-REQUIRED-SATISFIED).
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (queries, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-PREDICATE-NO-MATCH, ER-AGGREGATE-SKIP-COUNT, ER-ORDER-MARKERS-LAST, ER-GROUP-ONE-MARKER, ER-UNIQUE-IGNORES, ER-REFERENCE-MARKER, ER-CARD-ONE-READABLE-AND-ERASED, ER-EQUAL-SUPPORT-ERASED-CONFLICTS, ER-CARD-MANY-MARKERS-LAST, ER-REQUIRED-SATISFIED, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-RAW-HATCH. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.

**`G9.erasure.residual-shapes`: The Q52 shapes the pinned oracle does not model yet.**
- Statement: Per ERASURE queriesResidual, inFlight and commandShape (RULINGS Q52, provisional under the Q24 flag for Sam): a count of distinct values counts an attribute's erased values as one value (ER-COUNT-DISTINCT-MARKER, Q52a); ORDER BY puts readable values, then erased markers by assertion id, then missing values, in both directions (ER-ORDER-ERASED-THEN-MISSING, Q52b); a marker group reports the earliest erasedAt (ER-GROUP-EARLIEST-ERASEDAT, Q52c); an erased reference takes no part in reference constraints (ER-REFERENCE-CONSTRAINT-SKIPPED, Q52d); a read in flight across a commit erasing several values sees all old values or all markers, never a mix (ER-INFLIGHT-ALL-OR-NONE, Q52e); toDecimal(json, p, s, rounding) applies the named mode to the as-written reading and, without a rounding argument, excess digits are E-DECIMAL-FRACTION (DR-JSON-CONVERT-ROUNDING, Q52f); erasure is not an op and an erase mixed with other operations or given preconditions is a typed invalid-command error (ER-ERASE-COMMAND-SHAPE, Q52g); a read that started before n in-flight erasure commits sees one of the n + 1 prefixes (ER-INFLIGHT-PREFIXES, Q66a); a continuation cursor keeps its page's erasure prefix (ER-CURSOR-ERASURE-PREFIX, Q66b). O-REPLAY 0.4.1 refuses these shapes (ORACLE_REFUSALS q52-shapes), so this obligation stays blocked until 0.4.2 is accepted.
- Lanes: all four surfaces; receipt scope lane. Verifier mode: rerun.
- Cases: CS-ERASURE (residual, TO-AUTHOR); CS-ERASURE (ER-COUNT-DISTINCT-MARKER, ER-ORDER-ERASED-THEN-MISSING, ER-GROUP-EARLIEST-ERASEDAT, ER-REFERENCE-CONSTRAINT-SKIPPED, ER-INFLIGHT-ALL-OR-NONE, ER-ERASE-COMMAND-SHAPE, ER-INFLIGHT-PREFIXES, ER-CURSOR-ERASURE-PREFIX, TO-AUTHOR); CS-DECIMAL-ROUTING (DR-JSON-CONVERT-ROUNDING, TO-AUTHOR).
- Oracles: O-REPLAY (BUILT-ACCEPTED), O-ERR (COMPILED). Entrypoints: EP-WRITER, EP-REPO, EP-NATIVE, EP-RAW-HATCH. Profiles: P-TINY.
- Closure: CR-PASS-ALL; modes current, reopen; params {"provisional": true, "gates": ["GATE-ORACLE-PIN"]}.
